column1: Collections index for nonexistent user, work or collection shows all collections when it should 404
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h2. Steps to reproduce

# Go to the URL for the collections index of a work that does not exist, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/0000/collections|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/0000/collections]
# Go to the URL for the collections index of a user that does not exist, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/i_dont_exist/collections|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/i_dont_exist/collections]
# Go to the URL for the collections index of a collection that does not exist, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/i_dont_exist/collections|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/i_dont_exist/collections]

h2. What happens

For all three steps, you see a flash error that tells you that the work/user/collection doesn’t exist and are shown a listing of all collections.

h2. What should happen

You should be given a 404.

column27:
Only admins with the {{superadmin}} or {{policy_and_abuse}} role should be able to update and decline requests for invites by users.

Admins without those roles should:

* not have the “Manage Requests” option under “Invitations” in the admin navigation menu
* not have the “Manage Requests” in the admin navigation buttons on [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/invitations|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/invitations]
* be redirected and given an error message if they go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/user_invite_requests|https://test.archiveofourown.org/user_invite_requests]

h2. Testing

To test updating/declining requests, you may have to enable user invite requests in the admin settings and request invites as a user:

## Log in as an admin with the superadmin or policy_and_abuse role
## Follow the "Settings" link
## Check "Users can request invitations"
## Press "Update"
## Log out

## Hi, username! >  My Dashboard > Invitations > Request Invitations
## Fill in required fields
## Press "Send Request"
## Log out

column1: Upgrade to Rails 7.2
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Rails keeps on releasing new versions, and our current (7.1) goes EOL October 2025. So time to upgrade again!

Highlights from the Rails team:

* Development containers configuration for applications.
* Add browser version guard by default.
* Make Ruby 3.1 the new minimum version.
* Default Progressive Web Application (PWA) files.
* Add omakase RuboCop rules by default.
* Add GitHub CI workflow by default to new applications.
* Add Brakeman by default to new applications.
* Set a new default for the Puma thread count.
* Prevent jobs from being scheduled within transactions.
* Per transaction commit and rollback callbacks.
* Enable YJIT by default if running Ruby 3.3+.
* New design for the Rails guides.
* Setup jemalloc in default Dockerfile to optimize memory allocation.
* Suggest puma-dev configuration in bin/setup.

Requirements to upgrade, in broad strokes, are described in [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-7-0-to-rails-7-1|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-7-0-to-rails-7-1|smart-link]. There are probably also config changes that need post upgrade application, as is typical for new releases.

{{comment_notification}} and {{edited_comment_notification}} should be internationalized according to the [i18n standards|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Internationalization-%28i18n%29-Standards].

This includes [previews|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Developing-mailers#user-content-Mailer_previews] for the mailers. There are already a number of comment mailer previews. Make sure that there is at least one preview per mailer for each type of ultimate parent: work, tag and admin_post. There should also be a preview for a non-top-level comment, to cover the {{@comment.id == @comment.thread}} conditions in {{_comment_notification_footer}} (you may be able to combine this with other previews).

To make the previews' locale selector work, the {{I18n.with_locale}} block should be moved outside the mailer method, to where {{deliver_after_commit}} is called on the mailer. There should be cucumber tests for sending translated {{comment_notification}} and {{edited_comment_notification}} emails to a user to cover this change.

Please make sure that the email subject is covered by rspec tests, which should also check that there are no missing translations in the emails.

column1: Warn on login if current password is insecure
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
When a user or admin logs in, they should [receive a warning message|https://github.com/michaelbanfield/devise-pwned_password?tab=readme-ov-file#how-to-warn-existing-users-when-they-sign-in] if their password can be found in [HaveIBeenPwned’s database|https://haveibeenpwned.com/Passwords]. 

Users should also be redirected to the change password page ({{/users/USERNAME/change_password}}) so they can more easily act on the warning. (Admins don't have this page so should not be redirected.) 

Both parties should see the following message: 

{quote}Your password has appeared in a data breach from another site and is no longer secure. For your protection, please select a new, unique password.{quote}

h2. Testing

# A database admin should create or modify a user account and an admin account to each have the password {{password}}. 
# Log in as the insecure user. Make sure that you are redirected to the change password form with the above message. 
# Try to log in with an incognito/private window. You should also be redirected with the warning message.
# Change your password to something stronger (you can use an online generator). 
# Log in again. You should not be redirected to the change password form or receive the warning message.
# Log in as the insecure admin. You should receive the warning message. 
# Reset your admin password. You should be logged in and receive no warning message.
# Log in as a user with a strong password and make sure no message is displayed.
# Log in as an admin with a strong password and make sure no message is displayed.

column1: Blank values for past usernames and emails on user admin page
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
For accounts created during a certain period of time (at least 2016-2020), there are audits that show the login and emails being changed from {{nil}} to the user’s initial username or email. 

These nil values are included when we get {{@user.historic_values("email")}} or {{@user.historic_values("login")}} in the admin user show view ([/views/admin/admin_users/show.html.erb#L43-L57|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c1d52a8b76b1b76da4879f009d1e5f703e13d97a/app/views/admin/admin_users/show.html.erb#L43-L57]), so the page displays things like:

column1: Only permit email for password resets
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Background Since username is publicly visible, allowing someone to trigger a reset with that instead of email is a potential vector for harassment. Support and PAC have requested that we restrict resets to only be initiated by email. h1. Implementation We will need to update [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c1d52a8b76b1b76da4879f009d1e5f703e13d97a/app/controllers/users/passwords_controller.rb#L10|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c1d52a8b76b1b76da4879f009d1e5f703e13d97a/app/controllers/users/passwords_controller.rb#L10|smart-link] to only search by email, not email and username (AKA login). We should also update the checks for user existence and password resets over the configured limit to not allow email enumeration attacks (by not saying if a user is not found). To accomplish this, we will change all the status flash messages to a single message. The text for [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c1d52a8b76b1b76da4879f009d1e5f703e13d97a/app/views/users/passwords/new.html.erb#L10|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c1d52a8b76b1b76da4879f009d1e5f703e13d97a/app/views/users/passwords/new.html.erb#L10|smart-link] should also be updated, and it would be nice to change the form parameter from {{login}} (what we used to call username) to email, since it’s just that now. h3. Password reset page: {quote}

Reset Password

If you've forgotten your password, we can send you an email with instructions to reset your password.

Please enter the email address associated with your AO3 account. You may only request a password reset a limited number of times per day.

Email address _________________ [Reset Password]{quote} (Right now it’s 2 per email per 24 hours, but even when we change the threshold that message is close enough.) The browser title of this page should also be changed to “Reset Password” (currently it’s “New Password”). h3. Flash messages If you enter something that isn’t an email: {quote}You must enter your email address.{quote} If you enter something that looks like an email: {quote}If the email address you entered is currently associated with an AO3 account, you should receive an email with instructions to reset your password.{quote} h1. Testing # Find/create an account with an email address you have access to. # Go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/password/new|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/password/new]. # Make sure it only mentions email address, not username. # Try to trigger a reset by your account’s username. After submitting the form you should be on the reset password page with a “You must enter your email address.“ flash message. Check that you do not receive an email within about 15 minutes. # Try to trigger a reset by your account’s email address. After submitting the form you should be on the reset password page with a “If the email address you entered is currently associated with an AO3 account, you should receive an email with instructions to reset your password.“ flash message. Check that you receive an email within about 15 minutes with instructions on how to reset. # Repeat step 5 after an hour, another 15 minutes that, and after a day. Make sure that submitting the form always keeps you on the same page with the “If the email…” flash message and does not redirect you to another page. You should receive one more email. After that you should not receive another email until it has been at least 24 hours after the latest email.

column1: Allow admins to view anonymous and unrevealed blurbs on user's works in collections page
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h2. Steps: 

# Log in as a user with multiple works in different collections, some of which are:
## anonymous
## unrevealed
## neither anonymous nor unrevealed
# Go to your /works/collected page and observe the following:
## anonymous works are listed as Anonymous: TITLE by Anonymous
## unrevealed works are listed as Unrevealed: TITLE by USERNAME (or Anonymous if the collection is both anonymous and unrevealed)
## all other works are listed as TITLE by USERNAME
## the filter sidebar lists all of the collections that your works are in
# Log in as an admin
# Go to the same page as in step 2

h2. What happens:

You can only see the non-anonymous non-unrevealed works (2c), not the anonymous (2a) or unrevealed (2b) works. The filter sidebar only displays the collections that are neither anonymous nor unrevealed.

h2. What should happen:

You should be able to see all of the user’s collected works on this page, regardless of the visibility/status of the collection. The filter sidebar should display all relevant collections and you should be able to filter for just the works that are anonymous and/or unrevealed.

h2. Testing:

After making sure it shows all works on step 4, navigate to the unrevealed work’s collection. You should see Mystery Work on the blurb instead of the detailed blurb you saw on step 4.

column1: Disable phone number detection in iOS Safari
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Mobile Safari interprets numerical strings of certain lengths as phone numbers. This can cause links to appear in works, comments, and other pages on the site. 

[StackOverflow|https://stackoverflow.com/questions/226131/how-to-disable-phone-number-linking-in-mobile-safari] suggests the solution is to add the following to the site header: 

{{<meta name="format-detection" content="telephone=no">}}


We did something similar for Chrome as part of [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6565|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6565|smart-link] ([https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/commit/ceee061fbf9fccb38518129e65d3c36a0eace604|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/commit/ceee061fbf9fccb38518129e65d3c36a0eace604])



h2. Testing

Visit [https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1081354?show_comments=true|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1081354?show_comments=true] on an iPhone or iPad using the Safari browser. 

The numbers in the summary, work text, and comment should all be plain text.

column1: i18n comment_sent_notification
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
{{comment_sent_notification}} should be internationalized according to the [i18n standards|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Internationalization-%28i18n%29-Standards].

This includes [previews|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Developing-mailers#user-content-Mailer_previews] for the mailer. There are already a number of comment mailer previews. Make sure that there is at least one {{comment_sent_notification}} preview for each type of ultimate parent: work, tag and admin_post. There should also be a preview for an unreviewed comment on a work.

There should be cucumber tests for sending a translated {{comment_sent_notification}} email to a user.

Please make sure that the email subject is covered by rspec tests, which should also check that there are no missing translations in the emails.

h3. Testing Instructions

# Log in as a user whose emails you have access to
# Follow “My Preferences”
# Set “Your locale” to one of Українська, Ελληνικά or हिन्दी and save. *Only these three locales will work for testing!*
# Disable the “Turn off copies of your own comments.” setting
# Comment on someone else’s work
# You should get a {{Comment you left on ...}} email with a translated footer. The rest of the email will remain in English.
# For each of these mailer previews you should see an email without errors and without exposed HTML for both the text and HTML version:
## [https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/comment_mailer/comment_sent_notification_admin_post|https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/comment_mailer/comment_sent_notification_admin_post]
## [https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/comment_mailer/comment_sent_notification_tag|https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/comment_mailer/comment_sent_notification_tag]
## [https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/comment_mailer/comment_sent_notification_titled_chapter|https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/comment_mailer/comment_sent_notification_titled_chapter]
## [https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/comment_mailer/comment_sent_notification_untitled_chapter|https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/comment_mailer/comment_sent_notification_untitled_chapter]
## [https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/comment_mailer/comment_sent_notification_work|https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/comment_mailer/comment_sent_notification_work]
# Additionally, for [https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/comment_mailer/comment_sent_notification_work|https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/comment_mailer/comment_reply_sent_notification_work], selecting one of {{el}}, {{hi}} or {{uk}} from the locale dropdown should result in a preview with a translated footer. *Only these three locales will work for testing!*

h3. Deploy notes

The Resque workers need to be restarted.

The shadow should only be used on inputs where you enter text, not on checkboxes or radio buttons.

To illustrate the issue a little better, I’ve changed the shadow color to red for the attached screenshots.

h1. Deploy notes

Skins need to be recached.

column1: Can't set fallback by using the same CSS property multiple times in a single ruleset
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins > Create Site Skin
# Fill in a unique title
# In the CSS field, enter a ruleset that uses the same property multiple times with different values, e.g. {{.actions { background:#ddd; background:-webkit-linear-gradient(top,#fafafa,#ddd); background:-moz-linear-gradient(top,#fafafa,#ddd); background:-ms-linear-gradient(top,#fafafa,#ddd); background:-o-linear-gradient(top,#fafafa,#ddd); background:linear-gradient(top,#fafafa,#ddd) }}} 
#* This is something you’d do if you wanted to make sure older browsers that didn’t support unprefixed {{liner-gradient}} values also displayed gradients.
# Save

h1. What happens

Your skin only contains the last instance of the declaration:

{noformat}.actions {
  background: linear-gradient(top,#fafafa,#ddd);
} {noformat}

h1. What should happen

It should include all valid declarations, even if you’ve used the property before. 

h1. Notes

# It’s possible to work around this by creating one ruleset for each declaration, although this is unpleasant and not something we particularly want to do for skins we maintain.
# We have [a test that says it’s possible to do this|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/2271fae9856dc76d584df1a734a3a802b3ed713e/spec/models/skin_spec.rb#L107-L115]! However, the test is only checking that the CSS _saves_ – it doesn’t check the output to confirm all declarations are present. Since this doesn’t produce an error message and silently strips your fallback declarations, the test passes.

column1: Add series ID to work and bookmark blurbs
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Currently, {{.series-####}} only appears in the series blurb itself (i.e. when viewing a user’s dashboard or series page), not any works in that series or bookmarks of those works (i.e. when browsing tag listings or other pages containing blurbs of serialized works). We’d like to add this class to work and bookmark blurbs so that you can mute a series and not have to update your skin for each new work posted in that series. 

For consistency with the rest of the site, classes should probably appear in the order {{work-#### series-#### user-####}} 

h2. Testing

Note: When we check the styling, we’re using the dashboard because it updates almost instantly, while many other pages require reindexing. However, if you don’t see the expected results, wait a moment and refresh the page just in case there’s a slight lag.

# Post a work in a series
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required fields
## Check “This work is part of a series”
## Enter a title for your series in “Or create and use a new one:”
## Press “Post”
# Bookmark the work
## Press “Bookmark” to open the bookmark form
## Press “Create”
# Bookmark the series and make note of the series ID
## After you’ve created the bookmark, you’ll be on a page with the work blurb, which will contain a link to the series. Follow the link.
## Copy the series ID from the URL in your browser bar – you’ll need this for a later step
## Press “Bookmark Series” to open the bookmark form
## Press “Create”
# Create a skin that will highlight blurbs for the series, bookmarks of the series, works in the series, or bookmarks of works in the series by changing their background color
## Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins > Create Site Skin
## Fill in a unique title
## In the CSS field, enter {{.series-#### { background: plum !important; }}} to your site skin, using the ID from step 3b
## Press “Submit”
## Press “Use” to apply the skin
# Make sure the blurbs are styled correctly
## Hi, username! > My Dashboard
## In the “Recent works” section, the blurb for the work you created in Step 1 should have plum backgrounds
## In the “Recent series” section, the blurb for the series you created in Step 1 should have a plum background (while series already had the necessary classes, it’s a good idea to check that this change doesn’t affect the existing functionality)
## In the “Recent bookmarks” section, the blurbs for the bookmarks you created in Steps 2 and 3 should also have plum backgrounds
# Remove the work from the series
## Use the “Edit” link in the work blurb to access the work’s Edit page
## Under “This work is part of a series,” follow the “Remove Work from Series” link
# Make sure the blurb styles are updated
## Hi, username! > My Dashboard

We’d like to make the Draft feature more prominent, which may help reduce placeholders and/or duplicate works. (It’s not readily apparent when posting a new work or adding a new chapter that the Preview button will create a new draft work/chapter.) To that end:

# The “Save As Draft” button should be renamed to “Save Draft”, because whenever it currently appears, the draft already exists and you are not saving a _new_ draft, just editing/previewing your existing draft work/chapter. 
# The “Save Draft” button should also be added to the Post New Work form and the Add Chapter form. Clicking “Save Draft” should redirect you to the newly created work/chapter page (as it currently does when you click it from the Preview page). 
# The “Save Draft” button should not appear on works or chapters that have already been posted (but it should continue to appear when adding new chapters or editing/previewing existing draft chapters). 
# The “Post” button when editing anything that’s already posted should be changed to “Update”, since that’s what it does. (Currently it only says “update” when previewing the posted work/chapter/tags).
# The buttons on the forms should also be rearranged so the order/functionality is a little more consistent (aka Save Draft, Preview/Edit, Post/Update, Cancel)

column1: Prevent using a pwned password
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
To avoid later poor user experiences, we want to validate user (and admin) passwords to make sure they have not been leaked according to [HaveIBeenPwned’s database|https://haveibeenpwned.com/]. This does not (as of writing) require any API key.

We can use [https://github.com/michaelbanfield/devise-pwned_password|https://github.com/michaelbanfield/devise-pwned_password|smart-link]  to do this without writing our own validator by hand.

h1. Testing

# Try to sign up for a new account with the password {{password}}.
# Go to an existing account’s preferences and try to change the password to {{password}}.
# Go through the forgot password process and try to change the password to {{password}}.
# As an admin, go through the forgot password process at [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/password/new|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/password/new] and try to change your password to {{password123}} .

In all the above cases, you should receive an error that says the password is not secure and another one needs to be chosen.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Accessing a HTTP URL for AO3, e.g. [http://archiveofourown.org|http://archiveofourown.org], has a chance of a 520 error if the browser doesn’t automatically redirect to the HTTPS version. This happens most frequently when opening URLs from emails.

Let’s change emails to generate the HTTPS version of URLs to avoid the misbehaving browsers by setting the protocol in the {{default_url_options}} config for action mailer. Users that want to access AO3 via HTTP can continue to manually use the insecure subdomain.

# Do an something that generates an email, such as deleting your own work
# Check that all URLs in the resulting email begins with HTTPS

column1: Add automated test to check that fixtures used for database seeding result in valid records
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
The fixtures in {{test/fixtures}} are used to seed the development database with {{rake db:otwseed}}. These fixtures contain some invalid records such as creatorships without an associated creation. With [Gitpod|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Gitpod], the development database starts empty and is seeded every time a new development environment is created, so it is important that the initial seed data is valid and stays valid as we add more models and associated validations. So we should have an automated test for this.

column1: Allow basic use of custom properties/variables in site skins
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We’d like to allow the use of CSS custom properties, aka variables, aka {{--*}} in site skins! 

To test this, it would help to have some familiarity with [custom properties|https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_cascading_variables/Using_CSS_custom_properties] as well as our skin system.

h1. General

The help text for the CSS field on the skin create/edit page is updated to include this information after the “Font and Font Family” section: 

{quote}Custom Properties (Variables)

Custom property names can contain any combination of letters in the English alphabet in both uppercase (A-Z) and lowercase (a-z), numerals zero to nine (0-9), and underscores (_). 

They can’t contain single (') or double (“) quotation marks, or URLs.

All properties except font-family and content accept the var() function as a value. We don’t allow fallbacks.

Custom properties and the var() function are only available for site skins, and won’t work on work skins.{quote}

h1. Site skins

# Custom property names ({{--name}}) can include upper or lowercase letters A-Z, digits 0-9, underscores, and dashes. 
## Including a character that isn't allowed results in an error message: The [NAME] custom property in [SELECTOR] has an invalid name. Names can contain letters in the English alphabet in both uppercase (A-Z) and lowercase (a-z), numerals zero to nine (0-9), and underscores (_).
# Custom property values can be _almost_ any value you can use in site skins. 
## You can’t use single or double quotation marks, which we only allow in the values for {{font-family}} and {{content}}. Doing so results in our standard error message for invalid values: [PROPERTY] in [SELECTOR] cannot have the value [VALUE], sorry!
## You can’t use {{url()}}, which we only allow in {{background, background-image, border, border-image, list-style, list-style-image}}. Doing so results in our standard error message for invalid values: [PROPERTY] in [SELECTOR] cannot have the value [VALUE], sorry!
# You can use the variable function ({{var(--name)}}) as the value for any property except {{font-family}} or {{content}} (because values for {{font-family}} and {{content}} have different sanitization than what we use for everything else).
## Using {{var()}} for {{font-family}} results in our standard error message for invalid values: [PROPERTY] in [SELECTOR] cannot have the value [VALUE], sorry!
## Using {{var()}} for {{content}} results in our standard error message for invalid values: [PROPERTY] in [SELECTOR] cannot have the value [VALUE], sorry!
# You can use the variable function as _part_ of the value for properties that take multiple arguments, like {{box-shadow: 1px 1px 1px var(--name)}} or {{background: transparent var(--name)}}.
# You can only use _basic_ variable functions with one argument, i.e., {{var(--name)}} but not {{var(--name, #fff)}} or {{var(--name, var(--other_name))}}
## Using a fallback results in our standard message for invalid values: [PROPERTY] in [SELECTOR] cannot have the value [VALUE], sorry!

h1. Work skins

# Trying to define a custom property with a valid name gives the error: Custom properties are not allowed in work skins.
# Trying to define a custom property with an invalid name gives the error: The [NAME] custom property in [SELECTOR] has an invalid name. Names can contain letters in the English alphabet in both uppercase (A-Z) and lowercase (a-z), numerals zero to nine (0-9), and underscores (_).
# Trying to use the {{var()}} function gives the error: The var() function is not allowed in work skins.

h1. Deploy notes

Skins need to be recached (for the static help file).

12/Aug/25 12:23 AM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;[~accountid:557058:baa5f297-c116-4036-bbf1-109f8a7e50a7] It looks like CSSParser’s {{normalize_property}} method downcases property names as soon as we do {{parser.add_block!(css_code)}}, so there’s not a good way to look for custom properties containing capital letters. 

While we _could_ use a regex on the entire CSS string to look for any custom properties with capital letters before we get to add_block!, I think that’s probably slightly more kludgy than downcasing any {{var()}} functions we come across.

Downcasing the {{var()}} function will cause unexpected results if you have two variables that differ only in capitalization (eg {{--Whatever}} and {{--whatever}}), but a) why would you do that to yourself and b) you’d get unexpected results anyway because one of the definitions would get stripped. So especially given b), I think our best bet here is to add a note in the help file that all custom properties/variables will be converted to lowercase and then do that.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Create an anonymous and/or unrevealed collection
## Browse > Collections > New Collection
## Fill in required information
## Check “This collection is unrevealed” and/or “This collection is anonymous”
## Press “Submit” to finish creating the collection
# Update the anonymous or unrevealed setting

## Change “This collection is unrevealed” and/or “This collection is anonymous” (i.e., check one if it’s unchecked, or uncheck it if it’s checked)

h1. What should happen

For database admin troubleshooting purposes, the {{collection_preferences}} table should have two new columns, {{unrevealed_updated_at}} and {{anonymous_updated_at}}. 

When the anonymous or unrevealed setting is changed, the date and time of the change should be recorded in the corresponding column.

It’s fine if the new columns are initially set to the {{created_at}} date rather than nil – we’ll be able to see it’s the same as the collection_preference’s {{created_at}}. 

There should be no user-facing changes.

h1. Testing

Follow the steps above, and please provide the name of your collection, the approximate time you did Step 3, and which setting(s) you changed. A database admin will then confirm the data was recorded correctly.

We should also confirm that neither the {{unrevealed_updated_at}} nor {{anonymous_updated_at}} is affected if someone edits another setting, e.g., “This collection is moderated.”

This has a departure migration: {{rails db:migrate:up VERSION=20250816213210}}

column1: Gift and related work notifications sent for unrevealed works
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Note: You may want to split this into two issues: one for gift notifications and one for related works.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as UserA, who will receive the notifications (so make sure you have access to this account’s email address)
# Make sure UserA accepts gifts
## Hi, UserA! > My Preferences
## Check “Allow anyone to gift me works” if it’s not already checked
## Press “Update” to save if you’ve changed your preferences
# Post a work if UserA doesn’t have any – if they do, you can just make note of the URL
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required information
## Press “Post” to post the work
## Make note of the work’s URL
# Log out as UserA
# Log in as UserB
# Create two unrevealed collections
## Browse > Collections > New Collection
## Fill in required information
## Check “This collection is unrevealed”
## Press “Submit” to create the collection
## Make a note of your collection name/title
## Repeat to create a second collection
# Post a single work that is a gift to UserA, inspired by UserA’s work from Step 3, and in both collections from Step 6
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required information
## For “Gift this work to,” enter UserA’s name
## Check “This work is a remix, a translation, a podfic, or was inspired by another work”
## Enter the URL of the work from Step 3 in the URL field
## For “Post to Collections /  Challenges,” enter the names or titles of the collections you made in Step 6
## Press “Post” to post the work
# Reveal one of the collections (you have to do it this way due to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2240|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2240|smart-link] )
## Access your collection, e.g. by going to Browse > Collections and following the link to your collection
## Follow the “Collection Settings” link in the sidebar
## Uncheck “This collection is unrevealed”
## Press “Update” to reveal your collection

h1. What happens

UserA receives both a gift notification and a related work notification. However, UserA cannot access the work because it’s still unrevealed.

h1. What should happen

UserA should not receive any notifications. Notifications should only go out if a work is fully unrevealed.

08/Dec/25 12:04 PM;557058:baa5f297-c116-4036-bbf1-109f8a7e50a7;Due to text getting stored as its sanitized version, we cannot meaningfully distinguish between a {{<}} entered in a comment and a {{<}} entered in a comment. As an example, a comment made with the following text: {noformat}hi I point < to the left I point > to the right and I am just very bold text and I am escaped < less and I am escaped > more{noformat} results in the following string stored in the database: {noformat}

hi I point < to the left

I point > to the right

and I am just very bold text

and I am escaped < less

and I am escaped > more

{noformat} This means that simply replacing escaped HTML entities like {{<}} with {{<}} could lead to vulnerabilities if the email client parses the plain text email as HTML for any reason, as for example a comment from the user like {{< > <script>alert("evil")</script>}}, which is stored as {{

< > <script>alert("evil")</script>

}} in the database would become {{< > }}. So fixing this is not as simple as just decoding the HTML entities. From internal discussion, the approach we decided on was that we’d decode the HTML entities before we do strip_tags to make sure we remove things like {{<script>}} and then again after we strip_tags (since that will convert any & to & and so on). We’d rather deal with potentially missing content (like the script tag in the example) and be overly cautious than rely on email clients etc that parse the plain text email to really not parse those potentially malicious HTML tags.

column1: Skin.default doesn't always have the right attributes
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We use this code in the skin model for getting and/or creating the default site skin:

{code:ruby}  def self.default
    Skin.find_by(title: "Default", official: true) || Skin.create_default
  end

  def self.create_default
    transaction do
      skin = Skin.find_or_initialize_by(title: "Default")

      skin.official = true
      skin.public = true
      skin.role = "site"
      skin.css = ""
      skin.set_thumbnail_from_current_version

      skin.save!
      skin
    end
  end{code}

From {{create_default}}, you’ll note that the Default skin is supposed to be official and public, have no CSS, and have its {{role}} set to {{"site"}}. 

However, {{default}} is only looking for a skin that matches one of those conditions. If it finds such a skin, it’s happy! 

However, other parts of the code aren’t happy, because they rely on the other assumptions about the default skin. For example, there’s a [validation|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f767dd8e75020eae85ac31caf74e6c16a923fd45/app/models/skin_parent.rb#L11-L16] that means you can’t set its parent to Archive 2.0 unless it has the site or override role. Since this skin should be usable by everyone, you’re probably also not going to have a great time if the skin is {{public: false}}.

So, given that, let’s make it find {{Skin.find_by(title: "Default", official: true, public: true, role: "site")}}. If it doesn’t find a skin matching those conditions, it will update the existing skin titled Default or create a new one per {{create_default}}. 

(There may be legitimate reasons to include CSS in Default, so we won’t make that a requirement here.)

h1. Testing

This is probably fine with automated tests, but it wouldn’t hurt to make sure the default site skin is correctly loaded on a fresh Docker install.

column27:
Currently, if the link in a password reset email is invalid or was copied/entered incorrectly, the user doesn’t learn of this until after they fill out the form to set their new password. (Also “Reset password token is invalid” doesn’t make sense to users.)

We’d like the user to be told upfront that the link is bad (as soon as they visit the page/click the link in the email). Where possible, they should also be redirected to the password reset form ([https://archiveofourown.org/users/password/new|https://archiveofourown.org/users/password/new]) so that they can request a new reset if needed. 

# When no password reset token is provided ([https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/password/edit|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/password/edit] or [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/password/edit?reset_password_token=|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/password/edit?reset_password_token=]), you should be redirected to the password reset form with the error message:
## This password reset link is invalid or incomplete. Please check your email for the correct link or request a new password reset.
# When an incorrect password reset token is provided (you can use [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/password/edit?reset_password_token=RESET_PASSWORD_TOKEN|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/password/edit?reset_password_token=RESET_PASSWORD_TOKEN] for testing purposes) you should be redirected to the password reset form with the error message:
## This password reset link is invalid or expired. Please check your email for the most recent password reset link. If it has been more than {{ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_COOLDOWN_HOURS}} hours, you can request a new password reset.
# When a valid password reset token is provided, the user should see the set new password form. If you submit the form after the link has already expired, you should (not be redirected/remain on the same page and) receive the error message: 
## This password reset link is invalid or expired. Please request a new password reset instead.

h2. Testing

Only 1. and 2. need to be tested manually.

# Fill the “Chapter Title” field with “Some custom chapter title”
# Add some chapter content

In the PDF download, the chapter title of the first chapter is displayed as “Chapter 1”. The chapter title of the second chapter is displayed as “Some custom chapter title”.

In the PDF download, the chapter title of chapter 2 should be “Chapter 2: Some custom chapter title”. The chapter title of 1 should still be “Chapter 1”. This matches how chapter titles are displayed on the site itself.

We decided not to refresh the downloads cache for this change, so nothing special needs to be done.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Create a collection
## Browse > Collections > New Collection
## Fill in required fields

# Add a moderator to your subcollection
## Follow the “Membership” link
## Enter a username in “Add new members”
## Press “Submit”
## Choose “Moderator” from the select menu that corresponds with the user you just added
## Press “Update”
# Add the same user as an owner of the parent collection
## Parent Collection > Membership
## Enter the same username from Step 3b in “Add new members”
## Press “Submit”
## Choose “Owner” from the select menu that corresponds with the user you just added
## Press “Update”

h1. What happens

If you follow the Subcollections link, you’ll see the blurb for the subcollection. It will container the user’s name twice, since they are both an owner and a moderator.

If you access the subcollection and follow the Profile link in the sidebar, the “Maintainers” list also contains the user twice.

Both instances of the user’s name will have the {{owner}} class.

h1. What should happen

The user should only be listed once, with the {{owner}} class. The moderator role is irrelevant: having the owner role in the parent collection grants them owner privileges in the subcollection.

This is also true in reverse: if the user is an owner of the subcollection but a moderator of the parent, the moderator role is irrelevant in the subcollection because the user has owner privileges there. (In other words, they should have the {{mod}} class on the parent, but the {{owner}} class on the subcollection.)

column1: Text used by screen readers to announce help links is unclear
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27: h1. Steps to reproduce # Go to a page with help links, e.g. Search > Tags # Use Android TalkBack, NVDA, or another screen reader to interact with the help links h1. What happens The help link says, "question mark, link, Tag search text help, tap to activate" or similar, depending on the screen reader and the link. h1. What should happen It should say something a bit more comprehensible, like “[Descriptive text] link, tap to activate.” h1. Notes We use the [link_to_help method|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/108b55ac886496b69391e4bfee8f1bc4a46530df/app/helpers/application_helper.rb#L157-L168] for generating every help link. Each link is a question mark with a {{title}} attribute that's generated from the name of the file we load in the modal, e.g. {{tag-search-text-help.html}}: {noformat}? {noformat} That text is currently being read after the word “link” in our example, at least if your screen reader is set up to read {{title}} attributes. What we most likely need to do is replace the generated title attribute with an {{aria-label}} attribute that is written by humans. (Using something human-written will be helpful for localization as well.) Using {{aria-label}} should both prevent it from saying "question mark" and guarantee our preferred text is read. However, that's a bit of an undertaking given the ~50 places we use {{link_to_help}}, so it might be best handled by changing the {{title}} to {{aria-label}} and continuing to use the filename-based text if we don't provide something better. It will take a while to come up with a good naming system for the links, but we can make the underlying changes and add new link text in one location as a test/proof of concept. The Tag Search page, referenced in “Steps to reproduce”/”What happens,” has one help link for the “Tag name” field that can be used for this purpose. We can change the link name from “Tag search text help” to “Tag name search help.”

28/Nov/25 9:30 AM;712020:018354ff-23d8-4dc2-bb61-619c51c00e35;Can I suggest instead of this, we use {{aria-labelledby}}={the element adjacent to it}?

{{aria-label}} can be a bit of a code smell as it is verbalizing text not visible to a seeing user. In this case, it seems to me that the visual cue is the text element adjacent to the question mark (I’m assuming although I haven’t checked all the usages of this) and so that should be used to verbalize the link. We can have multiple elements in {{aria-labelledby}}, including the link itself, so it could say something like “Tag name, question mark, link”.

The main advantage of {{aria-labelledby}} is that if the element we’re referencing is localized properly, so will this, removing any need to provide human written text for translation. We would need to provide the id of the element we want this to reference (and ensure it has one which is a bit tedious), but if for some reason, we can’t do that, then perhaps we fall back to {{aria-label}}.

Because of that, {{aria-label}} works better for us than {{aria-labelledby}}.

column1: Focus not handled correctly when opening and closing modals
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Go to a page with help links, e.g. Search > Tags
# Use Android TalkBack, NVDA, VoiceOver, or another screen reader to interact with the help links and open the modal

h1. What happens

You have no idea new information has been added to the page.

Additionally, if you close the modal with the “Close” button or by pressing the escape key of your keyboard, focus is not returned to the help link you used to activate the modal.

h1. What should happen

The modal should receive focus and be announced when it is opened. 

Focus should return to the help link when the modal is closed. 

h1. Notes

We can use the modal’s title ({{_title}}) and content ({{_contentDiv}}) to help screen readers announce the modal. They’ll need ids like {{modal-title}} and {{modal-content}} that we can reference with {{aria-labelledby}} and {{aria-describedby}} attributes on the outermost container ({{_modalDiv}}).

If the modal does not have a title, the first heading should be used. (The titles of “first login help” and “share” modals will be removed in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7270|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7270|smart-link])

{{_modalDiv}} also needs two other attributes to help screen readers recognize it as a modal:

* {{‘aria-role': 'dialog'}} 
* {{'aria-modal': 'true'}}

While the current code attempts to put focus on {{_contentDiv}} once the modal is loaded ([ao3modal.js:109|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/108b55ac886496b69391e4bfee8f1bc4a46530df/public/javascripts/ao3modal.js#L109]), it isn’t successful because there’s no {{tabindex}} on that div. That could be solved simply by giving it a {{tabindex}}, but if it’s at all possible, it would be better to place focus on the first text element within {{_contentDiv}} – just keep in mind not all of our modals are the same, so you can’t rely on the first text element being, e.g., a particular heading level. 

You can read a bit about why a text element is preferable to the larger container element by checking out this [example of a modal dialog|https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/examples/dialog] (use the “Add Delivery Address” button to open the first modal and then the “Verify Address” button to open a second modal with more information about where to place focus).

Refer to [our JavaScript standards|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Coding-Standards#javascript] for info on working with minified files.

column1: Record when tags were last canonized and decanonized, let admins see it, and make it a sorting option on tag search
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Overview

We’d like to add two new {{datetime}} columns to the database for recording when a tag was most recently canonized or decanonized: {{canonized_at}} and {{decanonized_at}}. 

This information should be displayed to admins on tag edit pages (only admins with the {{superadmin,}} {{policy_and_abuse}}, or {{tag_wrangling}} admin roles can access this page). It should go directly under the information about when the tag was last updated and be written as “Last canonized on [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] UTC. Last decanonized on [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] UTC.” (If one is nil, the sentence can be omitted.)

{{decanonized_at}} and {{canonized_at}} should also be indexed in Elasticsearch so it can be used to sort tag search results by Date Canonized or Date Decanonized. (Canonizing or decanonizing a tag already prompts a reindex so you shouldn’t need to do anything extra there.) 

h1. Testing

# Log in as a tag wrangler
# Create a new tag and don’t do anything to its canonical status
## Browse > Tags > New Tag
## Fill in the “Name” field with the name of a tag that’s never been used before
## Choose a Category
## Press “Create Tag”
## Make note of the edit page’s URL
# Create a new canonical tag
## Browse > Tags > New Tag
## Fill in the “Name” field with the name of a tag that’s never been used before
## Check “Canonical”
## Choose a Category
## Press “Create Tag”
## Make note of the edit page’s URL
# Create another new canonical tag and then decanonize it
## Browse > Tags > New Tag
## Fill in the “Name” field with the name of a tag that’s never been used before
## Check “Canonical”
## Choose a Category
## Press “Create Tag”
## Uncheck “Canonical”
## Press “Save changes”
## Make note of the edit page’s URL
# Log out
# Log in as an admin with the {{superadmin}} , {{policy_and_abuse}}, or {{tag_wrangling}} admin role
# Find and decanonize a tag that was made canonical _before_ this was deployed
## Search > Tags
## Choose “Canonical” for “Wrangling status”
## Set “Sort by” to “Date created”
## Pick a tag from somewhere in the first few pages that isn’t huge and access its edit page
## Use the “last edited” information to verify it hasn’t been edited since this was deployed (if it has been, try again)
## Uncheck “Canonical”
## Press “Save changes”
## Below the “last edited” information, it should say, “Last decanonized on [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] UTC.” (Because it was canonized before this change, we don’t have information on when it was canonized.)
# Open the edit page for the tag from Step 4 that was canonized and decanonized
## Below the “last edited” information, it should say, “Last canonized on [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] UTC. Last decanonized on [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] UTC.”
# Open the edit page for the tag from Step 3 that was only canonized, 
## Below the “last edited” information, it should say, “Last canonized on [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] UTC.”
# Open the edit page for the tag from Step 2 that was neither canonized nor decanonized
## It should not say anything below the “last edited” information
# Log out
# Verify you can sort search results based on these dates
## Search > Tags
## Set “Sort by” to “Date Canonized”
## Set “Sort direction” to “Descending”
## Press “Search Tags”
## The results should list the tag from Step 4, the tag from Step 3, and then the rest
## Change the “Sort by” to “Date Decanonized”
## Press “Search Tags”
## The results should list the tag from Step 7, the tag from Step 4, and then the rest

h1. What happens

On the /participants page, the background of the section with people’s names will be lavender because it has the member class. 

There will be no background on the /people page because it does not have this class.

These lists contain the same people, known code-side as collection participants. Let’s make them have the same participant class, especially since member is a specific collection participant role.

## Fill in the other required fields
## Press “Preview” to create the draft

h1. What happens

When you go back to your assignments page (Hi, username! > My Assignments), your assignment will have the work title listed above some info about it: 

Status: Unposted Posted: 2025-09-25 Words: 4

This is slightly alarming because it seems like you posted your work.

h1. What should happen

The work title should be “Title (Draft)”

“Posted: YYYY-MM-DD” uses the work’s {{published_at}} date, which means just changing the label for a draft has its own potential for confusion, e.g. if you backdated your draft or update the publication date as you edit it. 

So for drafts, let’s display “Created: YYYY-MM-DD” using the {{created_at}} date. 

If that’s overly difficult given our various work dating issues, we can remove the “Posted” information for drafts instead.

column1: Number of collections in user sidebar is different from number of collections on user's collections page
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Create a collection
## Browse > Collections > New Collection
## Fill in required fields
## Press “Submit”
# Add another user as an owner of your collection
## Follow the “Membership” link from the collection’s Dashboard or Profile page
## In the “Add new members” field, enter the name of another user (ideally one with no collections, or just a couple)
## Press “Submit”
## In the list of member names, locate the select menu that corresponds with the user you just added and set their role to “Owner”
## Press “Update”
# Add a subcollection to the collection you created
## Browse > Collections > New Collection
## Fill in required fields
## For “Parent collection (that you maintain)”, enter the title of the collection you created in Step 2
## Press “Submit”
# Wait a minute or two for indexing to happen
# Go to the Collections page for your co-owner from Step 3: {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/collections}}

h1. What happens

Assuming the user had no collections to start with, the top of the page says they have 2 collections, and both of the collections you just made are listed on the page. However, the sidebar says “Collections (1).” 

h1. What should happen

The sidebar should say “Collections (2)”, the actual number of collections on the page.

h1. Notes

The sidebar count is currently coming from the database and doesn’t take into account inherited ownership/moderatorship (is that a word?) of subcollections the way Elasticsearch does. 

Instead of updating how we get the count from the database, let’s get it from Elasticsearch.

h1. Overview

We would like to add filters to the Collections pages for individual users (i.e., {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/collections}})! 

For maximum usefulness, the filters should have all the same options as the filters on the main Collections page. However, the results should be limited to collections the particular user maintains.

h1. Testing

To make sure that only the correct user’s collections are included in the results, you’ll need some collections that have the same filterable settings but different owners/moderators. 

(There’s probably enough data on staging to cover most fields if you’re using testy’s collections. The title field is the primary exception – it would be a good idea to use a different account to make a collection with the same title as one of testy’s collections.)

However, if for some reason you’re starting from scratch, these instructions will help ensure User A has collections they directly maintain, as well as subcollections that they only maintain through the parent collection:

# Create a collection as User A
## Log in as User A
## Browse >  Collections > New Collection
## At minimum, fill in required fields and enter one tag in “Collection Tags.”
### You might also wish to check “Multifandom,” “This collection is moderated,” “This collection is closed,” and/or set a “Type of challenge, if any.”
## Make note of the values you used in the aforementioned fields – you’ll be making additional collections with these settings.
## Press “Submit”
## If you selected a type of challenge, press “Submit” on that form as well.
## Log out
# Create a collection as User B using the same settings 
## Log in as User A
## Browse >  Collections > New Collection
## Fill in the fields using the values you noted down in Step 1d. (You won’t be able to reuse the name, but make sure to reuse the title.)
## Press “Submit”
## If you selected a type of challenge, press “Submit” on that form as well.
## Log out
# Create a collection as User C that _also_ uses the same settings, and that has User A as a moderator
## Repeat steps 2a-2f as User C
## Add User A as a moderator
### Follow the “Membership” link from the collection’s Dashboard or Profile page
### In the “Add new members” field, enter User A’s name
### Press “Submit”
### In the list of member names, locate the select menu that corresponds with User A and set their role to “Moderator”
### Press “Update”
# Still as User C, create a subcollection that also uses the same settings
## Repeat steps 2a-2f as User C one more time, but make sure to fill in “Parent collection (that you maintain)” with the collection from Step 3
## Log out
# Now as User D, repeat Steps 3-4, but make User B your moderator

And now, the things to check using the filters on User A’s (or testy’s, if you’re on staging) Collections page ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/collections}}):

# Selecting "Date Created" from "Sort by" should return the user’s collections ordered from 
## newest to oldest when "Sort direction" is set to Descending
## oldest to newest when "Sort direction" is set to Ascending
# Selecting "Title" from "Sort by" should return the user’s collections in 
## alphabetical order when "Sort direction" is set to Ascending (the default order on this page)
## reverse alphabetical order when "Sort direction" is set to Descending
# "Filter by title" should return expected results
# “Filter by tags” should return expected results
# Choosing a Closed option in the filters should return the expected results
# Choosing a Moderated option in the filters should return the expected results
# Choosing a Collection Type should return the expected results

column1: Spam check should include previous comments an individual has left on a given work/admin post
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Sometimes, spammers break their spam up by leaving multiple comments on the same work.

To help catch those, Akismet suggests the following:

{quote}If a commenter leaves an additional comment as a reply to the same comment that they've already commented on in the last ten minutes, include the text of the previous comments in the comment_content parameter and set recheck_reason to edit when you make your API call to Akismet. This more accurately reflects what they're doing (additional small edits to get their spam through).  If Akismet replies true to any of these calls, mark all of the comments that were included in the call as spam.{quote}

We’d like to tweak that a little:

* The timeframe should be configurable in config.yml.
* The check should occur when the same commenter leaves multiple comments on the work/admin post within the configured timeframe, not just when the comments are in a single thread.
* Likewise, the comment_content sent to Akismet should include the text of all comments that the commenter left on the work/admin post within that timeframe, not just comments within a given thread.

Additional notes:

* We use a validation to determine if a comment is spam, which isn’t an appropriate place to update existing records. The controller might be a better alternative.
* For the purposes of this spam check, we will treat comments as being by the same commenter if the comments are
** associated with either the same email address or the same IP. (Since we’re limiting it to comments in the last X minutes, the odds of accidentally ensnaring a non-spammer with the same email or IP are relatively low.)
** from the same new (as defined by AO3-6933), logged-in user. 

h1. Testing

# As a guest, use the same email to leave several (2-3) top-level comments on the same work or admin post within the configured timeframe. The final comment you leave should have the text “viagra-test-123” and it should be flagged as spam and result in your previous comments being hidden.
# Repeat Step 1 using the same IP address but different emails on multiple comments.
# Create a new account and use it to leave several top-level comments on the same work or admin post within the configured timeframe. The final comment you leave should have the text “viagra-test-123” and it should be flagged as spam and result in your previous comments being hidden.
# Repeat Steps 1-3 leaving several comments in the same thread.
# For bonus points, repeat Steps 1-3 leaving several comments in different threads (i.e., as replies to different users who have already commented on the work).

column1: Can't pick skin from chooser in footer without Javascript
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h2. Steps to reproduce

# Disable javascript
# Log in as a user
# Log out
# Log in as a different user
# Use one of the skin links in the footer to set your current skin (do not use the “Default” link)

h2. What happens

You get an auth error and the skin is not set.

h2. What should happen

You get a success message that the skin is set and you remain on the same non-error page.

h2. Development notes

This is caused by the {{button_to}}s for the skins links [being cached in the footer|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/d476d0cf5835e9d59257f4c75b1c7260907a9f52/app/views/layouts/_footer.html.erb#L6-L18], because this caches the authenticity token for the post action between different users. We should switch to caching only the skin titles and the {{Skin#to_param}} that we need for the links and always reconstructing the buttons from the cache, similar to what we did for the links in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7020|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7020|smart-link]. It would be nice to avoid the N+1 query for loading the skins when caching this data.

Additionally, this cache is expired [every time any skin is saved|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/d476d0cf5835e9d59257f4c75b1c7260907a9f52/app/models/skin.rb#L62-L64]. It would be much more efficient to only expire it when a skin that is in the chooser is modified, or a skin is added to/removed from the chooser.

column1: Record user ID field for abuse reports of series
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
When an Abuse report is submitted for a series ({{/series/####}}), it should include the user IDs of the series creator(s) in the field {{cf_user_id}}. This should not be transmitted via a hidden field on the abuse report form, but rather handled in the controller/model as appropriate. 

* Multiple IDs should be separated by a comma and listed in ascending numerical order
* A given ID should be listed only once, regardless of how many pseuds the user has on the series
* The IDs should be included even if the user is no longer a creator of any specific work in the series
* The IDs should be included even if (one of the works in) the series is anonymous or unrevealed 
* If one of the creators is orphan_account, replace orphan_account’s ID with the placeholder {{orphanedseries}} (it should come before any other user IDs)
* If the series is deleted, the ID field should say {{deletedseries}}

h2. Testing: 

Someone will need to submit reports for the following and PAC will need to verify the expected information is available and correct for:

* subpages (works page, profile page, etc)
* pages belonging to any of the user’s pseuds ({{/users/USERNAME/pseuds/PSEUDNAME}} and its subpages)
* the user's or pseud’s filtered works or bookmarks page ({{/works?PARAMETER&user_id=USERNAME}} or {{/bookmarks?PARAMETER&user_id=USERNAME}})

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Turn off sending a referer header in your browser’s debug settings (e.g. in Firefox this is a about:config item) or use an alternative URL to access the archive
# Log into an account with a least one comment in the inbox
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard
# Follow the “Inbox” link in the sidebar
# Select a filter (e.g. “Show without replies”)
# Press “Filter”
# Select a comment
# Press one of “Mark Read”/”Mark Unread”/”Delete From Inbox”

h2. What happens

A 500 error.

h2. What should happen

You get redirected to your previous inbox page with the same search filter applied.

h2. Development note

The error is {{ActionController::UnfilteredParameters unable to convert unpermitted parameters to hash}} and raised in [inbox_controller.rb:50|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/01e33e3d5ee9c467650bf93689402f1723983c51/app/controllers/inbox_controller.rb#L50]. Please fix this by replacing the mass {{permit!}} in {{filter_params}} with a proper {{permit}} for the right parameters and then reuse those permitted filter parameters for the redirect.

h2. Testing

It should be fine to rely on automated tests for this since the setup is rather convoluted in the browser on staging but trivial in rspec tests.

column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Create a pseud
## Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Profile > Manage My Pseuds > New Pseud
## Fill in Name
## Press Create
# Create a collection
## Browse > Collections > New Collection
## Fill in required fields
## Press “Submit”
# Add your pseud as a member of your collection and update its role
## Follow the “Membership” link from the collection’s Dashboard or Profile page
## In the “Add new members” field, enter the name of another user (ideally one with no collections, or just a couple)
## Press “Submit”
## In the list of member names, locate the select menu that corresponds with the user you just added and set their role to “Owner”
## Press “Update”
# Remove your pseud from the collection
## Press the “Remove” button that corresponds with your pseud
## Press “OK” when the confirmation message asks, “Are you certain you want to remove pseud?” 

h1. What happens

After Step 4e, the success message just says, “Updated pseud.” (Where “pseud” is your pseud, of course.)

In Step 5b, the confirmation prompt asks, “Are you certain you want to remove pseud?” and the success message after pressing “OK” says, “Removed pseud from collection.” (Again, where “pseud” is your pseud, of course.)

This is confusing if the pseud matches the username of another collection member, or if you are used to the normal way we format pseuds.

h1. What should happen

It should say “pseud (username)” instead of “pseud” in all these places. 

Additionally, the confirmation message should say “Are you sure” instead of “Are you certain”

column1: Allow collections to be sorted by number of works or bookmarked items

h1. Overview

On the Collections page, the filters should have “Bookmarked Items” and “Works” in the “Sort by” filter, after the existing “Date Created” and “Title” options. (If you check the “Sort by” options on work filters, the options aren’t in alphabetical order – the various countable stats-type things are last.)

Choosing one of those options should sort the results in descending order, using the public or general (logged-in) counts as appropriate. 

h1. Testing

This assumes you don’t have any data and are trying to manually test this on a dev environment. 

On staging, you can use the existing collections and ensure things are sorted as expected while you are logged in, logged out, and logged in as an admin.

# Log in
# Make two collections
## Browse > Collections > New Collection
## Fill in the required fields, which we’ll call Collection 1 (make note of the name and title you actually use)
## Press “Submit”
## Repeat to make a second collection, which we’ll call Collection 2
# Post two restricted works to the first collection
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required information
## Check “Only show your work to registered users”
## Use the autocomplete to fill in “Post to Collections / Challenges” with Collection 1
## Press “Post”
## Repeat to post a second work to the collection
# Post a public work to the second collection
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required information
## Use the autocomplete to fill in “Post to Collections / Challenges” with Collection 2
## Press “Post”
# Wait a minute or two for Elasticsearch to update
# Sort collections by works while logged in
## Browse > Collections
## From “Sort by,” choose “Works”
## Press “Sort and Filter”
## Verify that Collection 1 (2 works) is the first result and Collection 2 (1 work) is the second
# Sort collections by works while logged out
## Log out
## Repeat 6a-6c
## Verify that Collection 2 (1 work) is the first result and Collection 1 (0 works) is the second
# Sort collections while logged in as admin
## Log in as admin
## Repeat 6a-6d
## Log out
# Log in
# Add a bookmark of a public work to the first collection
## Access the public work from Step 4
## Press “Bookmark”
## Use the autocomplete to fill in “Post to Collections / Challenges” with Collection 1
## Press “Create”
# Add bookmarks of two restricted works to the second collection
## Access the first restricted work from Step 3
## Press “Bookmark”
## Use the autocomplete to fill in “Post to Collections / Challenges” with Collection 2
## Press “Create”
## Repeat with the second restricted work from Step 3
# Wait a minute or two for Elasticsearch to update
# Sort collections by bookmarked items while logged in
## Browse > Collections
## From “Sort by,” choose “Bookmarked Items”
## Press “Sort and Filter”
## Verify that Collection 2 (2 bookmarked items) is the first result and Collection 1 (1 bookmarked item) is the second
# Sort collections by bookmarked items while logged out
## Log out
## Repeat 13a-13c
## Verify that Collection 1 (1 bookmarked item) is the first result and Collection 2 (0 bookmarked item) is the second
# Sort collections by bookmarked items while logged in as admin
## Log in as admin
## Repeat 13a-13d

h1. Notes

If [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7143|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7143|smart-link] is done first, these options should also be available on user pages. 

We already use the collection ID as a secondary sort option to avoid having the same result appear on multiple pages a la [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6291|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6291|smart-link].

h1. Overview

Occasionally, a user applies a skin that’s so broken they can’t access the “Revert to Default Skin” button. 

Support used to work around this by giving them a direct link to unset their skin: {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/skins/unset}}. However, this is no longer possible due to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5953|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5953|smart-link]. 

To make up for this, admins with the {{support}} or {{superadmin}} role should be able to go to the user’s Preferences page and change the user’s skin using the “Your site skin” select menu. (They should be able to select any option, not just Default.)

h1. Testing

As the user whose preferences will be edited:

# Create a site skin
## Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins > New Site Skin
## Fill in required fields
## Press “Submit”
## Make note of the skin’s title for the {{support}} or {{superadmin}} admin

As an admin with the {{policy_and_abuse}} role:

# Go to the user’s preferences ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/preferences}})
# Choose a skin from “Your site skin”
# Press “Update”
# You should be redirected to the homepage with an error message saying only an authorized admin can access the page you were trying to reach

As an admin with the {{superadmin}} or {{support}} role:

# Go to the user’s preferences ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/preferences}})
# Choose a public skin (e.g., Reversi) from “Your site skin”
# Press “Update”
# You should get a success message saying preferences were successfully updated
# Ask the user to confirm their skin has changed
# Repeat Steps 1-5, this time choosing “Default” from “Your site skin”
# Repeat Steps 1-5 one more time, this time choosing the non-public skin the user created

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins > Create Site Skin
# Enter the following CSS: {{.test-2 { v^lue: blue; }  .test-4 { color: p^nk; }  .t^st { fakeproperty: blue; }}}
# Press “Submit”

h1. What happens

The error message you get:

Sorry! We couldn't save this skin because: 

* lue -- please notify Support if you think this is an error. 
* There don't seem to be any rules for .test-2. 
* nk, sorry! 
* There don't seem to be any rules for .test-4. 
* We don't currently allow the CSS property fakeproperty -- please notify Support if you think this is an error.
* st.

h1. What should happen

The error message you wish your error message could look like:

Sorry! We couldn't save this skin because: 

* We don't currently allow the CSS property v^lue -- please notify Support if you think this is an error. 
* There don't seem to be any rules for .test-2.
* color in .test-4 can't have the value p^nk, sorry! 
* There don't seem to be any rules for .test-4. 
* We don't currently allow the CSS property fakeproperty -- please notify Support if you think this is an error. 
* There don't seem to be any rules for .t^st.

h1. Notes

The ^ is allowed in skins and should be – the problem is it has special meaning when used in Rails error messages. 

Refer to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6320|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6320|smart-link] for an example of somwhere we dealt with this in the past.

column1: Improve sidebar navigation accessibility
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Overview

The navigation sidebar that is included on various pages should be converted from a {{div}} with the {{role="navigation"}} attribute into {{nav}} elements and given distinct labels and landmark headings.

h2. Notes

* The labels and landmark headings serve different purposes, so including both is good.
* When labeling {{nav}} elements, you don’t want to include the word “navigation.” Most assistive tech will add the word “navigation” right after the label name, so it is annoying and redundant.

h1. Testing

The easiest thing to do will be check the page source and ensure the elements are present (or not) as expected.

h2. Admin posts

[https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts] 

#  This is already a {{nav}} and should continue to be a {{nav}}.
#  {{role="navigation region"}} should be removed from the {{nav}}. 
# If you’re on the index, the sidebar contains a page summary. We should label the {{nav}} by referencing its existing (invisible) “Page Summary” {{h3}} using the {{aria-labelledby}} attribute.
# If you’re on an individual news post, the {{nav}} contains a list of recent admin posts. We should change the “Page Summary” {{h3}} on these pages to “Recent News” and use it to label the {{nav}}.

h2. Collections

[https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/COLLECTION_NAME|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/COLLECTION_NAME]

# {{div}} should be converted to a {{nav}}.
# {{role="navigation region"}} should be removed.
# {{aria-label="Collection"}} should be added.
# The invisible {{h3}} should be changed from “Dashboard” to “Collection Navigation.”
# An invisible “About” {{h4}} should be added before the first group of links in the sidebar. (The other {{ul}} elements already have {{h4}} headings and it is confusing for it to be missing from one section, especially when that section starts right below an {{h3}}.)

h2. Tag Wrangling

[https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags] while logged in as a wrangler

# {{div}} should be converted to a {{nav}}.
# {{role="navigation region"}} should be removed.
# {{aria-label="Tag Wrangling"}} should be added.
# An invisible “Tag Wrangling Navigation” {{h3}} should be added as the first element inside the {{nav}}.
# An invisible “General” {{h4}} should be added before the first group of links in the sidebar.
# An invisible “Uses” {{h4}} should be added before the second group of links (which starts with “Works (#)”) in the sidebar on [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/edit|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/edit]
# An invisible “Children” {{h4}} should be added before the second group of links (which starts with “Characters (#)”) in the sidebar on [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing]
# An invisible “Mass Bins” {{h4}} should be added before the second group of links (which starts “Fandoms by media (#)”) on [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=fandoms|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=fandoms]

h2. User

[https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME]

# {{div}} should be converted to a {{nav}}.
# {{role="navigation region"}} should be removed.
# {{aria-label="User"}} should be added. 
# An invisible “User Navigation” {{h3}} should be added.
# To avoid confusion, the {{nav}} in the header that contains “Hi, username!” and so on should have its label changed to “Account.”

column1: Chapter and download menus cut off
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
You’ll need

* a device with a small screen, e.g. a tablet in portrait mode or a phone in either portrait or landscape mode
* a work with two or more chapters, ideally with titles that are more than a few words long

Depending on the width of your device, the arrangement of links in the work navigation, the length of the chapter title, and/or the font size, when you open the Chapter Index or Download menu, the menus may run off the edge of the screen.

For example, if I access [https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1070791/chapters/2224588|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1070791/chapters/2224588] while logged out on an iPhone 14 Pro, the menus both extend off the left side of the screen:

!IMG_6339.jpg|width=566,alt="The Chapter Index and Download menus running off the left side of the screen."!

While the first chapter of the same work shows the menus fully on screen because “Next Chapter” is shorter than “Previous Chapter”, so the “Chapter Index” button is on the right of the top line instead of the left of the second line:

!IMG_6340.jpg|width=566,alt="The Chapter Index and Download menus fully on screen."!

To stop this, we want to make sure the menu isn’t any wider than the button it belongs to when our midsize or narrow stylesheets are applied. That means the items in the menus will stack vertically (the background won’t be purple in the finished product):

!IMG_6338.jpg|width=566,alt="The Chapter Index and Download menus only as wide as their parents, with options stacked vertically."!



The behavior on wider screens, like laptops, should be unchanged.

h2. Deploy notes

Skins need to be recached.
