column1: Low Vision Default: Chapter menu cut off
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
You’ll need

* a device with a small screen, e.g. a tablet in portrait mode or a phone in either portrait or landscape mode
* a work with two or more chapters, ideally with titles that are more than a few words long

Log in on your small screen device, access the multichapter work, and then scroll down to the footer and select the “Low Vision Default” skin.

Depending on the width of your device, the arrangement of links in the work navigation, the length of the chapter title, and/or the font size, when you open the Chapter Index menu, the menu may run off the edge of the screen like so:

!lvd_menu.png|width=478,alt="Chapter menu running off the left side of the screen in Low Vision Default"!

To stop this, we want to make sure the menu isn’t any wider than the button it belongs, just like we did with the default skin on small screens for [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7195|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7195|smart-link]

!lvd_fix.png|width=523,alt="Low Vision Default with the chapter menu staying on screen."!

Don’t use Samsung Internet or Opera on an Android phone to test due to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7201|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7201|smart-link]

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h2. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Post > New Work
# Fill in the required fields
# Press "Post"
# Press "Add Chapter"
# Change the chapter number to an invalid value:
## Something that is not a number (e.g. “abc”)
## Zero or a negative number
## A number greater than the total number of chapters (including the one being posted)
# Press "Post"

h3. What happens

The chapter is posted.

h3. What should happen

The form should display an error and prevent posting the chapter.

h2. Notes

We would like to have both backend and live validations on the chapter position.

There are existing works with chapters that have out-of-range positions. We will also need a rake task to fix the chapter numbers of those works to ensure that they can still be modified in the future.

h3. Testing Instructions (Rake Task)

A database admin will need to break the chapter positions of a work with at least 3 chapters. This can be done like so:

{noformat}chapters = work.chapters_in_order
chapters[0].update_column(:position, 0)
chapters[1].update_column(:position, 1)
chapters.last.update_column(:position, chapters.length + 1){noformat}

After doing so, check the chapter index of the work to ensure that the chapters are now numbered incorrectly. Make note of the order of the chapters.

Then, run the rake task and recheck the chapters to confirm:

* The relative ordering of the chapters was maintained
* The chapters are numbered starting from 1 with no gaps and no duplicates.

h3. Deploy Notes

Run the rake task, TBD.

21/Jan/26 11:55 AM;62a561f4f8bd790069d6251d;So, I got about a quarter of the way through manually copying strings when I thought “you know, this could probably be automated and go a lot faster.” I then spent the next several hours in a AuDHD fugue state, spending more time on the tool than I would’ve just doing it by hand.

!https://imgs.xkcd.com/comics/automation_2x.png|width=250!



But in the end, I came up with [a vaguely horrifying pair of Ruby scripts|https://gitlab.com/hunteradasmith/otwarchive-help-file-migrate-tool#] that may make future help file migrations a lot faster. It parses a help file and extracts strings of text and interpolatable tags (e.g. {{<a>}}, {{<code>}}, {{<strong>}}) and dumps them to an intermediate YAML file. You can then enter I18N keys for each string. Then the tool will take the intermediate file, update the main {{en.yml}} with the strings, and generate and ERB template.

In my limited testing, it seems to work decently enough to get ~80% of the work done. Manual work is needed from there to fix edge cases, correct formatting, and validate and test.

Dunno if anyone might find it useful, but thought I’d throw it out there.

When we index users in Elasticsearch for admin search, we include some data from the audits table. Some users have a lot of data in that table – like 100k rows of it – which causes it to choke and tie up user-facing indexing jobs (e.g., work indexing).

We’d like to move user indexing to a separate queue named {{reindex_users}} so any logjams there won’t affect user-facing parts of the site.

Requires a worker and scheduler restart on staging.

# Log in as an admin who can search for users (i.e., an admin with one of these roles: {{superadmin legal policy_and_abuse open_doors support tag_wrangling}})
# Manage Users > Find Users
# Make sure the user turns up in search results

25/Dec/25 7:08 PM;712020:ce34ae37-af2b-4f47-a1b8-dec561ebfce3;I don’t want to claim this ticket until I get a working solution. But I wanted to document what I’ve done in case someone can get an acceptable fix faster than I can. This is what I’ve found so far:

# Identified where the bug is happening -[ line 194 in works_controller|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/controllers/works_controller.rb#L194C6-L194C98] redirects the user to the full work view {{if params[:view_full_work] || (logged_in? && current_user.preference.try(:view_full_works))}}. When a user who has {{view_full_works}} preference turned on makes a comment in a chapter by chapter view, it redirects to {{params[:view_full_work] = “false”}} to preserve that chapter by chapter view. However, {{”false”}} is truthy. And even if {{”false”}} was falsey, we would still fall back to the user’s preference.
# I updated this line to {{if params[:view_full_work] == "true" || (logged_in? && current_user.preference.try(:view_full_works) && params[:view_full_work] != "false")}} to be explicit. This solution works to keep the user in chapter by chapter mode but *_introduces a new bug_*
# The new bug is that when a user leaves a comment, they get redirected to the top of the page. It looks like the change above is not playing well with the logic to set an anchor in the comments_controller. [I suspect there’s an issue with redirect_to_all_comments|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/controllers/comments_controller.rb#L681] in the comments_controller, which gets called as part of the [comment create path|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/controllers/comments_controller.rb#L385]
column132:
27/Dec/25 3:39 PM;712020:ce34ae37-af2b-4f47-a1b8-dec561ebfce3;Got a working solution but also uncovered another bug. 

# Go to work with 39 comments (or whatever the pagination limit is)
# Add the 40th comment
# Instead of getting redirected to the comments section, user is redirected to the top of the work page



This happens because we use anchors to navigate users back to the comment section. Since we use pagination, and comments are sorted by created_at, the most recently written comment is in page 2 and _not_ visible on the work page. Since the anchor id is not visible in the html, when a user writes a comment, the following happens:

# POST comment
# After writing a comment, gets redirected to the the work url which looks like this {{work/:id?<query_params>#comment_id}}
# Element with id = comment_id is not visible on the page due to pagination
# Since the anchor tag does not exist on the page, user stays at the top of the work page

column1: Allow certain admins to download existing copies of hidden or unrevealed works
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
When a work is hidden by an admin or placed in an unrevealed collection, the Download button is removed. Because the button is now inaccessible, if any download files were generated prior to the work being hidden/unrevealed, it is not easy to access those stored copies. 

We’d like to keep the Download button available to admins with the {{policy_and_abuse}} and {{superadmin}} roles only. Clicking the button on hidden/unrevealed works should only download a copy of the work if a download file was generated prior to the work being hidden/unrevealed; if there is no existing download file in the requested format, then no file should be created/downloaded.

This should be implemented without any modifications to the downloads controller. Instead, we will rely on cached downloads to be returned and simply don’t hide the link to them.

Note: Downloading a PDF/EPUB/MOBI/AZW3 also generates an HTML file, which is used to create the other formats.

h2. Testing

# Post a new work (version 1) in an unrevealed collection. As the work creator, you should not see the Download button on your unrevealed work. 
# Log in as a {{superadmin}} or {{policy_and_abuse}} admin. You should see the Download button, but clicking it should not result in downloading the work no matter which format you choose.
# As the work creator, take the work out of the collection. 
# Click Download > EPUB. You should receive an .epub file of version 1 of the work.
# As a {{superadmin}} or {{policy_and_abuse}} admin, hide the work. 
# Click Download > EPUB. You should receive an .epub file of version 1 of the work (identical to the file you received in step 4).
# Click Download > HTML. You should receive an .html file of version 1 of the work.
# Click Download > PDF. No files should be downloaded. 
# As the work creator, you should not see the Download button on your hidden work. 
# As a {{superadmin}} or {{policy_and_abuse}} admin, unhide the work.
# As the work creator, edit the work to contain different text (version 2).
# Click Download > PDF. You should receive a .pdf file of version 2 of the work.  
# Edit the work again to contain different text (version 3). 
# As a {{superadmin}} or {{policy_and_abuse}} admin, hide the work.
# Click Download > PDF. You should receive a .pdf file of version 2 of the work (identical to the file you received in step 12).
# Click Download > HTML. You should receive an .html file of version 2 of the work.
# Click Download > EPUB. You should receive an .epub file of version 1 of the work (identical to the file you received in step 4).
# Click Download > MOBI. No files should be downloaded.

column1: Track past emails and usernames via a separate table
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Context

In [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6565|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6565|smart-link], we started indexing past usernames and emails for users in Elasticsearch so admins can search by them. The implementation scans the audits of a user, which is very bad performance for older user accounts that have many thousands of audit entries (due to the structure, an index on a few columns can’t help).

We do plan to clean these up, but we can improve performance even more by specifically logging the information we care about in separate tables. This also gives us another benefit: we can clean up the audits table without worrying about losing search information.

h1. Data Model

We want 2 new tables: {{user_past_emails}} and {{user_past_usernames}}, each with a corresponding model. They both should have a {{belongs_to}}relationship to {{User}} (the {{users}} table).

||*Column Name*||*Column Type*||*Notes*||
|user_id|bigint|Can be a foreign key; that plays badly with our online migration utility, but hopefully the version of MariaDB with built-in online migrations will be deployed soon…|
|email_address / username|string|Depends on the table (should match the name)|
|changed_at|datetime|Set to the date that the email or username was changed to something else (said another way, the time at which this username/email was last effective)|
|created_at|datetime|Default Rails timestamp field|
|updated_at|datetime|Default Rails timestamp field|

h1. Code Changes

# On username and email change, log a row into the appropriate table created (details above)
## When emails are changed, they should only be logged when the new address is confirmed. This should have an automated test.
## If possible, the change and logging should be part of the same transaction to avoid misleading “past” information.
# Create a script to backfill based on the {{audits}} table.
## _For performance reasons, this needs to be asychronous via a Resque queue._ {{utilities}} should be fine.
## This should limit the number of audits we scan, like in [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/5491/changes|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/5491/changes|smart-link] , to avoid problems. (The impact should be less, but we should still not risk it.)
## Backfilling should not create duplicate information if it was already recorded between the new code being deployed and the backfill script being run. This should have an automated test.

h1. Deploy notes

* -Make sure the pre-deploy testing step is done!- ✅ 
* Has pre-deploy migrations: {{rails db:migrate:up VERSION=20260103083335}} and {{rails db:migrate:up VERSION=20260103083447}}
* Deploy
* Needs a worker restart
* Run the backfill script {{bundle exec rake After:backfill}}

h1. Testing

# Find a user that has username and email changes. Note the current and past values.
# Deploy the code, run the migration(s), and run the backfill script. This needs to be AD&T or Systems.
# Change a user’s email and username.
# Ask a database admin to check that the past username/emails were recorded and older values backfilled.

column27:
The underlying cause of these problems is the same – admin activities are created before the code checks if the edit is not a preview and valid – so they are grouped together.

h1. Invalid edits

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as an admin with one of these roles: superadmin or policy_and_abuse
# Access a work through whatever means you like, e.g., go to Browse > Works and follow the link to a work
# Follow the Edit Tags and Language link
# Remove all of the fandom tags
# Press “Update,” which will result in an error message
# Go to the Activities page

h2. What happens

Even though pressing “Update” results in an error, there is a new item in the Activities table.

h2. What should happen

There should not be an item added to the Activities table.

h1. Canceling an edit

# Log in as an admin with one of these roles: superadmin or policy_and_abuse
# Access a work through whatever means you like, e.g., go to Browse > Works and follow the link to a work
# Follow the Edit Work link
# In the “Rating” field, choose a new rating
# Press “Preview”
# Press “Cancel”
# Go to the Activities page

h2. What happens

Even though you canceled the edit, there is a new item in the Activities table.

h2. What should happen

There should not be an item added to the Activities table.

column1: Improvements to the work over-reporting limit
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Currently, reports of any URL containing {{/works/####}} get checked against the {{ArchiveConfig.ABUSE_REPORTS_PER_WORK_MAX}} and {{ArchiveConfig.ABUSE_REPORTS_PER_WORK_PERIOD}} reporting limits. This can cause issues when a URL contains this string but the page is not actually about the work itself. 

For example, when viewing specific comments from your inbox, the URL is in the format {{/works/####/comments/####}}, which can result in being unable to report multiple comments on the same work and/or being unable to report a work if enough comments on that work were previously reported such that the work-reporting limit has already been reached. 

To make it easier to test this, let's make the default values for the work reporting limit 3 times per 30 days and give works their own error message "This work has already been reported. Our volunteers only need one report in order to investigate and resolve an issue, so please be patient and do not submit another report." instead of the generic "This page has already been reported" message. 

The work-specific error message should display for reports of: 

* work links such as {{/works/####}} or {{/collections/NAME/works/####}}
* work links with parameters or anchors such as {{/works/####?show_comments=true}} or {{/works/12345#kudos}}
* chapter links such as {{/works/####/chapters/####}} or {{/chapters/####}}
* work-related subpages such as {{/works/####/navigate or /works/####/comments}}

However, reports of the following pages should NOT result in receiving a "This work has already been reported." error message (depending on the status of other issues, you may get no error or another error such as "This comment has already been reported"): 

* specific comments {{/works/####/comments/####}} 
* specific bookmarks {{/works/####/bookmarks/####}} 

h2. Testing

# Post a work. 
# Go to your Preferences page and ensure that "Turn off messages to your inbox about comments." is unchecked.
# Log out and post two comments on the work (as a guest or as a different user).
# Log back in as the work creator. 
# Navigate to your inbox and right-click on the work title links to open both comments in new tabs. The URLs should both be in the format {{/works/####/comments/####}}.
# Report the first comment via the {{/works/####/comments/####}} URL repeatedly – you should not get an error message containing the word "work".
# Report the work repeatedly until you get the "This work has already been reported" error message.
# Report the second comment via the {{/works/####/comments/####}} URL – it should go through. 
# Try to report the work repeatedly via various links such as {{/works/####/chapters/####}} or {{/works/####?show_comments=true}} - you should get the "This work has already been reported" error message each time.

h1. Overview

It should be

* easier to locate the published date for chapters, which is currently only listed on the Chapter Index
* easier to locate the comment count for chapters, which is currently only provided in the Comments link on the bottom of the chapter
* possible to determine the word count for chapters

To do this, we will

* add a Chapter Stats section to the work meta that contains those pieces of information, in the same order they are presented in the existing Stats section (Published, Words, Comments, with Comments only included when comments are present)
** the Chapter Stats section will only be included if the work has multiple chapters accessible by the person visiting the chapter (e.g., if the work has one posted chapter and one draft chapter, a random user/guest will not see a Chapter Stats section, since you can infer the same information from the work’s word count, comment count, and updated date)
** the Chapter Stats section will not be included in Entire Work mode
* add the word count to the Chapter Index
* rename the Stats section of the work meta to Work Stats to better distinguish the two

h1. Testing

Note: The stats aren’t cached and use existing methods, so you don’t really need to test things like “does the publication date change if I change it,” “is the word count for this chapter right,” or “does the comment count include unreviewed or spam comments,” but you’re welcome to.

The current default password lengths in config.yml are

{noformat}PASSWORD_LENGTH_MIN: 6
PASSWORD_LENGTH_MAX: 40
ADMIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH_MIN: 10
ADMIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH_MAX: 40{noformat}

This is extremely short, so let's increase it to 8-72 for users and 10-72 for admins. (The 72 comes from the upper limit imposed by bcrypt.)

The password live validation messages (on the account creation page) should also be edited to say "characters" rather than "letters", since we accept a wide range of Unicode.

### Try to change to a password that is above 72 characters. You should get an error message that your password is too long.

column1: Allow different rate limits to be applied based on the current user
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We can use the {{rate_limit}} method introduced in [Rails 7.2|https://api.rubyonrails.org/v7.2.3/classes/ActionController/RateLimiting/ClassMethods.html#method-i-rate_limit] to apply more granular rate limits based on context available to the app, such as the current user account’s age. Note: This method gains more functionality in [Rails 8.0|https://api.rubyonrails.org/v8.0.4/classes/ActionController/RateLimiting/ClassMethods.html#method-i-rate_limit], which is not available to us yet!

We’d like to set this up for creating and editing comments. The following conditions should be applied to the rate limit:

* Limit by user ID. Guests are not affected by this limit
* The limit is shared between creating comments and editing comments, meaning someone limited from editing also cannot create new comments
* Only new users are rate limited, the age for a new user is defined by the {{account_age_threshold_for_comment_spam_check}} admin setting
* Exclude user's comment on a work they created from the rate limit
* Exclude comments on tags from the rate limit

Users who are rate limited *with JavaScript off* should be redirected to a new 429 error page. Users who are rate limited with JavaScript on will not see any specific error, the “Comment” button will simply not work. (This may be improved in a separate Jira issue.)

The text for the new error page is the following, with appropriate HTML tags for paragraphs/heading similar to other error pages in the ErrorsController:

{noformat}Error 429
Too Many Requests

You have made too many requests in a short time period. Please wait a while before trying again.

If you are receiving this error repeatedly, try browsing more slowly or loading fewer pages at a time.{noformat}

For testing, the rate limits included in the PR should be 3 comments per 15 minutes. These rate limits should be configurable in the config file. The period for the rate limit should be in seconds, to match our rack attack configuration.

h2. Deploy notes

This needs a new Redis instance, {{redis_rate_limits}}. Be aware of the following from the Rails documentation: “Deployment note: Take care to use a *dedicated Redis cache* rather than pointing this at a persistent Redis server (for example, one used as an Active Job queue). Redis won’t cope well with mixed usage patterns and it won’t expire cache entries by default.”

The production configuration for {{RATE_LIMIT_USER_COMMENTING_NUMBER}} and {{RATE_LIMIT_USER_COMMENTING_PERIOD}} needs to be updated before deploying to production.

h2. Testing instructions

-The AD&T volunteer transitioning this issue into QA should make sure that the “How old (in days) accounts should be before we stop checking comments for spam” admin setting on Staging is set to some value between 5 and 30.-  ✅ 

# As a guest, find a work that allows guest comments
# On that work, make or edit 4 guest comments within 15 minutes. All comment creations/edits should be successful (you may have to change up your wording to not hit the spam filter)
# Create a new user account at [https://test.archiveofourown.org/signup|https://test.archiveofourown.org/signup] and log in (make sure to remember the password and username)
# Post a work that allows commenting
# On the work you posted, make or edit 4 comments (including some replies) within 15 minutes. All comment creations/edits should be successful (you may have to change up your wording to not hit the spam filter)
# Find a work that you haven’t created that allows comments
# Within the next 15 minutes, do the following:
## On that work, make 4 comments, including some comment replies (you may have to change up your wording to not hit the spam filter). The fourth comment should not save
## Attempt to edit one of the comments. The edit should not save
## Log out
## Create a new user account at [https://test.archiveofourown.org/signup|https://test.archiveofourown.org/signup] and log into that account
## Navigate to the previous work
## Leave a comment on the work. It should save
# Wait 15 minutes
# Log into the account from Step 3
# Leave a comment on a work that user didn’t create. It should save
# Turn off javascript
# Create new comments on the work until you hit the rate limit again. Upon hitting the rate limit, you should be redirected to the 429 error page described above.
# Edit comments on the work until you hit the rate limit again. Upon hitting the rate limit, you should be redirected to the 429 error page described above.

column1: Comment action buttons don't display for admins/guests on comment URLs with reply parameters
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h2. Steps to reproduce

# Post a new work and set it to “Registered users and guests can comment”.
# Log out and comment on the work as someone else. 
## If commenting as a guest, use an email you have access to.
# Check your (creator’s) email for the comment notification and right-click to open the “Reply to this comment” link in a private browsing window. 
# Log in as an admin and view the above link.
# Log in as the creator and reply to the comment.
# Set the work to “Only registered users can comment”.
# Check your (commenter’s) email for the comment reply notification and right-click to open the “Reply to this comment” link in a private browsing window. 
# Log in as an admin and view the above link.

h2. What happens

Guests can see the reply form in step 3, because the work still allows guests to comment. In step 7 when commenting is restricted, they see the comment but it’s missing the Thread button. 

Admins cannot see any of the buttons they would usually see on comments (thread/hide/freeze/spam/delete/etc), and have to manually remove the {{?add_comment_reply_id=####}} parameter from the link in order to take action on the comment. 

h2. What should happen

Admins should always be able to hide/freeze/spam/delete the comment regardless of additional URL parameters. Guests should always be able to see the Thread button, even though they can’t reply. This matches what each party sees when viewing comments on the work itself or the direct comment links without the reply parameters. 

This should be solved by not setting {{display:none}} for the comment actions in [/app/views/comments/_comment_actions.html.erb#L3|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b23fe624793956ce5fbf2612dfe2e3456704797b/app/views/comments/_comment_actions.html.erb#L3] if {{can_reply_to_comment?}} is false for the comment.

column1: Unreviewed comments marked as spam are still visible to creators
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h2. What happens

When a creator marks a guest comment on their work as spam, it is removed from view + their inbox and the comment count immediately decreases. (Admins can still see the spam comment when viewing the work, but not the creator’s inbox.) 

However, if the comment was unreviewed when the creator marked it as spam, it only vanishes from the inbox. On the Unreviewed Comments page, the creator sees the guest comment with a banner “This comment has been marked as spam.” (which is what an admin sees). The number of comments displayed on the Unreviewed Comments button does not decrease (unless the creator deletes or approves the spam comment. If they approve it, it does not show up for them on the work, only for admins).

h2. What should happen

Marking unreviewed comments as spam should make them invisible to creators and decrease the comment count, same as when regular comments are marked spam. 

Admins should continue to be able to access the Unreviewed Comments page and see any unreviewed spam comments, even if there are no unreviewed comments visible to the creator. The comment count for admins should continue to display the total number of unreviewed comments (regardless of spam status), as it does now.

h2. Testing

# Post a new work with the settings “Registered users and guests can comment” and “Enable comment moderation” selected.
# Log out and comment on the work twice as a guest. 
# Log in as the creator and view your work. The button at the top should say “Unreviewed Comments (2)”.
# Click on the button to go to the Unreviewed Comments page. You should see 2 comments. 
# Click on the “Spam” button for one of the comments and confirm you want to mark the comment as spam. 
# You should be redirected to your work. Confirm that the button says “Unreviewed Comments (1)”.
# Navigate back to the Unreviewed Comments page. You should only see one comment. 
# Mark the remaining comment as spam. The Unreviewed Comments button should no longer appear on your work. 
# Log in as an admin with the superadmin, board, policy_and_abuse, or support role and navigate to the work. The Unreviewed Comments button should be visible and it should say that there are 2 comments. 
# Click on the button to go to the Unreviewed Comments page. You should see 2 comments, both with blue banners declaring that they have been marked as spam. 
# Mark one of the comments as “Not Spam”. 
# You should be redirected to the work. Confirm that the button still says “Unreviewed Comments (2)”.

column1: Editing work to be published in the past does not always set work as backdated
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h2. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Post > New Work
# Fill in the required fields
# Press “Post”
# Press “Edit”
# Check “Set a different publication date”
# Set a different publication date. Pick a very early date, e.g. in the 1950s
# Uncheck “Set a different publication date” again
# Press “Update”
# Wait 5-10 minutes for the work to be reindexed
# Hi, username! > My Works
# Fill “Search within results” with “backdate:false” (without the quotes)
# Press “Sort and Filter”
# Navigate to the last page of the search results

h2. What happens

The work is shown in the search results as posted a long time ago. (You may have to view the work and look at the date on the meta, not just the date on the blurb in the results.)

h2. What should happen

The work should not be backdated if “Set a different publication date” it not checked when submitting the edit form, to match what happens when you post a work. The work should still be shown in the search results for “backdate:false”, but it should be shown as posted recently when it was originally posted, not in the 1950s.

h2. Coding notes

This is an issue with the record in the database, meaning “backdate” is not set to true on the work (because the checkbox was unchecked), not an issue with Elasticsearch. This can also be reproduced by disabling JavaScript and not checking “Set a different publication date” at all, so the solution for this should not rely on Javascript resetting the date when the checkbox is unchecked.

The dates on the blurb and meta may not match, that problem is described here: [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6288|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6288|smart-link]

column1: Speed test for allowed number of Tag offers in Gift Exchanges
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
When creating a new gift exchange, the “Requests and Offers” section, the “Request Settings” section and the “Offer Settings” section has fields for maximum number of allowed items for each type of tag (Fandom(s), Character(s), etc.), that number is currently limited to a maximum of 20. This restriction predates the rewrite of the matching algorithm to improve its performance. 

We are uncertain if 20 is a randomly selected number, is based on the limitations of the previous matching algorithm, or is a necessary cap even for the current matching algorithm. We would like to run some speed tests to clear this up. Specifically, we want to know if it’s possible to increase the maximum for offered tags, we don’t want to change the maximum for requests. 

*Methodology*

Feel free to change this based on your observations on what would create the best measurements.

* Create baseline numbers for a small, medium and large gift exchange with the current limits.
* Then run these again but with the allowed number of offers increased. Realistically we are looking at an increase to 25 or 30, but you can test this with a bigger number if you think it provides insight.
* Obviously there is a lot of variation in possible signups, which has an effect on the numbers. For this test it is fine to randomise the number of offers. Run the test in benchmark mode to ensure the randomness does not create too much variety in outcomes.
* It may be necessary to test with and without tag sets

*Outcome*

Please share the results of your tests in this issue. If the result is that the number of allowed tags can’t be raised without negatively affecting performance, please add a code comment saying that this must stay at 20 with a reference to this issue. If the result is that changing this number has no effect on performance, increase the number by 5 or 10, pick which based on your results.

column1: Asynchronous reveal of collection works/creators runs even after collection is set back to unrevealed/anonymous
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h2. What happens

# Create an unrevealed/anonymous collection
# Post a work to the collection
# Something or someone unintentionally changes the collection preference to be revealed/non-anonymous
# Before the async task runs and reveals anything, a collection moderator very quickly notices the incorrect preference and changes the collection back to unrevealed/anonymous
# The async task runs and reveals the works/creators, despite the collection being set to unrevealed/anonymous at the time the task runs
# Panic!
# A collection moderator manually goes through the collection items and sets each of them back to unrevealed/anonymous
# The async task failed executing and was put into the failed task Resque queue. Some time later, someone looks at the failed task queue and reruns all failed tasks
# Due to the async task getting rerun, the works/creators reveal again, despite the collection being set to unrevealed/anonymous at the time the task runs
# Even more panic!

h2. What should happen

Less panic. Change the asynchronous reveal/creator reveal tasks to not reveal anything if the collection has been changed back to unrevealed/anonymous in the time between the task getting queued and executed.

h2. Deploy notes

Needs a worker restart.

h2. Testing

This can’t easily be tested because on Staging async Resque tasks get executed almost immediately (on account of the queue being basically empty), so rely on automated tests instead.

column1: Configurable number of shards for pseuds and tags index

Similar to how the number of shards for the user, collection, works and bookmarks indexes are [configurable in config.yml|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b23fe624793956ce5fbf2612dfe2e3456704797b/config/config.yml#L776-L781], the number of shards used by the tags and pseuds indexes should also be configurable.

column27:
After the changes in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7251|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7251|smart-link]  there are N+1 queries in the UserIndexer:

{noformat}       expect do
         UserIndexer.new(User.ids).index_documents
       end.to perform_constant_number_of_queries
     
       Expected to make the same number of queries, but got:
         10 for N=2
         12 for N=3
       Unmatched query numbers by tables:
         user_past_usernames (SELECT): 2 != 3
         user_past_emails (SELECT): 2 != 3{noformat}

This can be prevented by updating the {{klass_with_includes}} in the indexer. We should also have an automated test for the N+1 queries.

Needs a worker restart.

Bullet doesn’t flag the number of queries produced during background jobs, so there’s no way to check the number of queries in QA. That said, it would be good to test that this indexer is still working.

column1: Create Ability to Mass Un-Assign Fandoms from Tag Wranglers
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
In order to help with workflow for both individual wranglers and admin wranglers, we need to be able to remove fandoms more efficiently. 

At present the way fandom removal works is:  

# A user with wrangling permissions goes to: [https://archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers|https://archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers] 
# This page by default lists all fandoms alphabetically with the wranglers assigned to them filed under each fandom with an x next to their name. 
# To remove the fandom assignment from a wrangler, any wrangler can click the x button and this will cause the wrangler to be removed from the fandom and the page to reload. 
# This page additionally allows lookup of fandoms by what they start with (search box) and can be filtered to show only fandoms in a certain media or fandoms assigned to a specific wrangler.  

How we would like mass unassignment to work is:

For each individual wrangler's page (Example: [https://archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers/Ao3_Catch_and_Release|https://archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers/Ao3_Catch_and_Release][)|https://archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers/Dreary_MidnightTW)] to feature a check box next to the assigned fandoms on the page and an unassign button at the bottom of the page which would allow a wrangler to go through and check the box next to each fandom they wish to unassign and then click the unassign button to mass unassign those checked fandoms from themselves. 

Ideally this would operate similar to the last wrangled date function in that this option on the page would only be visible to the user whose wrangling page it is and to TW admins, but if that makes the design or implementation significantly more challenging, we would be perfectly happy even it if these options were visible to anyone with wrangling permissions.

If it’s significantly less heavy lifting, alteration of aspects of the [https://archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers|https://archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers] showing wrangler view (example: [https://archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers?media_id=&wrangler_id=Ao3_Catch_and_Release&fandom_string=&commit=Filter|https://archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers?media_id=&wrangler_id=Ao3_Catch_and_Release&fandom_string=&commit=Filter]) to allow for similar mass-unassign functionality would also be fine. The main need here is just a method by which Supervisors and individual wranglers can more easily unassign multiple fandoms. 

Have attached screenshots of relevant pages for reference.

column1: Adding Additional Filtering Options to Tag Search
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We’re hoping to add to additional options to the Wrangling status options on [https://archiveofourown.org/tags/search|https://archiveofourown.org/tags/search|smart-link] 

*Current Options are:*

* Canonical
* Non-Canonical
* Synonymous
* Canonical or synonymous
* Non-canonical and non-synonymous

*Additional Options We’d Like Added Are:*

* Non-canonical and non-synonymous and not marked unwrangleable
* Unwrangleable

As it would be useful for searches to be able to view all tags that have been marked as “unwrangleable” as well as to be able to filter out tags which have been marked as “unwrangleable” in addition to those which are Non-canonical and non-synonymous (the point of this last option to have a search option which filters for only tags that haven’t been actioned in some way).

h2. Testing Instructions

# Log in as a tag wrangler (e.g. testy)
# Hi username! > Tag Wrangling
# Come up with a unique prefix to name tags with (e.g. ‘ABC123’, so that it’s easy to filter results)
# Create a new non-canonical tag
## Select “New Tag” in the sidebar
## Fill in “Name” with “<prefix> Unactioned”
## Select a category.
## Press “Create Tag”
# Create an unwrangleable tag
## Select “New Tag” in the sidebar
## Fill in “Name” with “<prefix> Unwrangleable”
## Select a category.
## Press “Create Tag”
## Check “Unwrangleable”
## Press “Save Changes”
# Create a canonical tag
## Select “New Tag” in the sidebar
## Fill in “Name” with “<prefix> Canonical”
## Select a category.
## Check “Canonical”
## Press “Create Tag”
# Create a synonymous tag
## Select “New Tag” in the sidebar
## Fill in “Name” with “<prefix> Synonymous”
## Select the same category as the canonical tag (step 6).
## Press “Create Tag”
## Fill in “Synonym of” with “<prefix> Canonical”
## Press “Save Changes”
# Search > Tag
# Ensure that all tags have been indexed
## Fill in “Tag Name” with the prefix you used to name all the tags
## Press “Search Tags”
### All four tags (Canonical, Synonymous, Unactioned, Unwrangleable) should appear in the results
# Filter for unactioned tags
## Select Wrangling status: “Non-canonical and non-synonymous and not marked unwrangleable”
## Press “Search Tags”
### Only the “Unactioned” tag should appear in the results
# Filter for unwrangleable tags
## Select Wrangling status: “Unwrangleable”
## Press “Search Tags”
### Only the “Unwrangleable” tag should appear in the results

column1: Regularly Set Bookmark Tags That Have Been Assigned a Fandom Back to Unsorted
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
In general, tag wranglers do not wrangle bookmark tags so these tags should remain Unsorted until such time as they are used on a work posted to the Archive. However, sometimes, bookmark tags will be assigned a tag category for a variety of reasons and are sometimes wrangled to fandoms which isn’t really helpful to either users or wranglers. 

Consequently, we are requesting a regular reset of bookmark tags to Unsorted to remove them from bins and reset any category assignments that have been visited upon them. It would be helpful if this could run quarterly, but if that’s not feisible we would be fine with once every six months or once a year as the most important thing is just having it run on a regular basis at whatever cadence is reasonable for y’all. Thank you.

h1. Testing

h2. Set up

# Log in as a tag wrangler (e.g., testy)
# Create a "Dirty" Tag (The Target) that should be cleaned up by the rake task
## Browse > Tags > New Tag
## In the Name field, enter a name that has never been used before (e.g., {{Test Dirty Bookmark Tag AO3-7294 A}})
## Select an option from Category (e.g., Character)
## Press “Create Tag”
## Check the sidebar and make sure it says Works (0)
## In the “Fandoms” field, enter a canonical fandom (e.g. {{Testing}})
## Press “Save changes”
## Save the URL of this page (the tag edit page) for later
# Create a “Control” Tag (The Innocent) that should not be touched by the rake task
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required fields
## In the Relationships, Characters, or Additional Tags field, enter a tag that has never been used before  (e.g., {{Test Control Tag AO3-7294 A}})
## Press “Post”
## In the work meta, locate your new tag, and click on it to access its tag landing page
## Follow the Edit link
## In the “Fandoms” field, enter a canonical fandom (e.g. {{Testing}})
## Press “Save changes”
## Save the URL of this page (the tag edit page) for later

Ask a database admin to run {{bundle exec rake tags:reset_bookmark_only}}

h3. Verify results

# Use the URL from Set up Step 2h to access the tag edit page for the dirty/target tag and confirm that
## the Category select menu is now set to UnsortedTag
## there is no Fandom information
# Use the URL from Set up Step 3i to access the tag edit page for the control/innocent tag and confirm that
## the Category is still set
## the Fandom is still set

column1: Remove unused and insecure reset_word_counts task
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
The {{reset_word_counts}} task in {{work_tasks.rake}} is not safe to run because the {{content_will_change!}} call leads to active record callbacks marking the content as sanitized with the latest sanitizer version, but doesn’t actually resanitize the content. This happens via [ApplicationRecord#update_sanitizer_version|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/22bc0c98149a979856e672d24145b237ad31b85e/app/models/application_record.rb#L5-L13]. This is a security concern as of [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4382|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4382|smart-link]  which changed the sanitizer version to no longer always be {{1}}.

Fixing this task to resanitize the content or recalculate the word count in some other way may be difficult (due to performance concerns related to the now much larger size of AO3) and we currently have no plans to rerun this task. It was only run once, when it was originally created in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2378|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2378|smart-link] . So we’re instead opting to remove it (despite [previously|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6433] deciding against that). 

This issue was discovered as part of [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6787?focusedCommentId=372246|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6787?focusedCommentId=372246|smart-link] which had the same issue, as well as performance issues.

column1: De-duplicate work/chapter notice logic
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
There are 3 notices that can be displayed at the top of the work and chapter show pages: a draft deletion notice, unrevealed work notice, and co-creator invite notice. Currently, the checks to display each notice are duplicated in the two files. We’d like to move the three notices into a partial (named {{works/work_notices}}) so that they can be shared between the work and chapter pages.

In addition, the content from the {{works/work_unrevealed_notice}} partial can be copied directly into the new partial (with the old file deleted), since it’s not used anywhere else.

h3. Testing Instructions

# Have two users prepared, A and B
## Ensure that user B has the “Allow others to invite me to be a co-creator.” preference checked
# Log in as user A
# Create an unrevealed collection
## Browse > Collections
## Press “New Collection”
## Check “This collection is unrevealed”
## Check “Add co-creators?”
## Add user B to the list of co-creators
## Fill in required fields
## Press “Submit”
# Create a draft work in the collection
## Press “Post to Collection”
## Fill in required fields
## Press “Save Draft”
## Press “Save Draft”
# Add a draft chapter to the work
## Press “Add Chapter”
## Fill in required fields
## Press “Save Draft”
## Press “Save Draft”
# Log in as user B
# Navigate to the draft work made in step 4
## Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Co-Creator Requests
## Follow the link to the draft work
# You should see three notices:
## “This work is a draft and has not been posted. The draft will be *scheduled for deletion* on <date>”
## “This work is part of an ongoing challenge and will be revealed soon! You can find details here: +<collection name>+”
## “You've been invited to become a co-creator of this work. To accept or reject the request, visit your +Co-Creator Requests page+.”
# Press “Next Chapter”
# You should see the same three notices as in step 8.

column1: Statistics: when a graph tooltip is under the cursor, it flickers
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h2. Steps to reproduce

The exact steps depend on the amount of works you have and their statistics.

# Log in
# Have at least 1 work posted
# Go to the Statistics page (My Dashboard > Statistics)
# Find a graph where the tallest column is tall enough that its tooltip appears in front of it and not above it. 
## The subscriptions one might be the easiest to use on staging, if it’s empty then you can subscribe to one on your works yourself and the resulting graph should work.
## Otherwise you should also be able to make a column tall enough by adding words to the work with the most words.
# Put your cursor over the tooltip (like in the screenshot):
## If using a mouse, hover over the column so that your cursor is in front of both the column and the tooltip.
## If using a touchscreen, tap the column and tap the tooltip in a place where it overlaps with the column.

!image-20260222-200357.png|width=525,alt="image-20260222-200357.png"!

h2. What happens

The tooltip flickers, making it difficult to read.

h2. What should happen

The tooltip should stay in place and not flicker.

h2. Notes

CSS that should fix this:

{code:css}.statistics.chart svg > g:last-child {
    pointer-events: none;
}{code}

This is caused by [a bug with the Google Visualization API|https://github.com/google/google-visualization-issues/issues/2162] used for the graphs.

The user in question isn’t even very old. Ultimately, this results in a low-level (and unintentional for now) denial of service due to a huge load on the audits table. To fix this, until the PR linked above is released in a proper version of Devise, let’s fork the main release branch and cherry-pick the fix.

column1: Audits cleanup job
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Context

User changes are currently stored in the {{audits}} table. These are important to committees like PAC, but we don’t need to store it infinitely – and at the moment, the table is so big that it’s painful to change, even via a tool like {{pt-online-schema-change}}.

h1. To-Do

To improve that, let’s create a scheduled job that removes audits that are greater than 4 years old.  However, that value should be configurable. This job should be scheduled via the Resque Scheduler (not a rake task) to run every month. *We also want to skip* {{create}} *and* {{destroy}}*events for now*; bonus points if we can configure a second threshold for those that when set to zero/a negative number ignores them for deletion.

We also need to have an {{AdminSetting}} that can store a (small) list of user ids that should not have their audits cleaned up in case of a legal hold. This setting should be accessible to superadmins, Policy & Abuse admins, and Legal admins. Other admin roles should not be able to access the current state of the setting, meaning it should be hidden on the admin settings page.

*Note for AD&T reviewers:* ask Systems to help check the query to make sure it’s safe to run initially. If not, we may need to create an index or do something a bit hacky to get the initial cleanup done.

h1. Testing

# *Before deploying to staging*
## Find a user with audits going back more than 4 years.
## Note the username.
# *Right after deploying to staging* (before the job can run)
## Update the admin setting to prevent cleaning up audits for the user from 1b.
# As a normal user (PAC or AD&T admin help required)
## Log in and change your username, email, or password.
## Ask an AD&T or Systems person to manually kick the job (to not wait a month).
## Have AD&T and/or PAC check the audits for your account.
## The information should still be there.
## (As an AD&T admin) change the audits for the account from step 1 to have a timestamp of 5 years ago. Run the job again.
## The audits should now be gone.
# As the deployer
## Check that the audits for the account from step 1b are still present.

h1. Deploy notes

The migration *must be run before deploy*. On Staging, where that is not possible, run {{AdminSetting.first.recache_settings}} after running the migration.

column1: Collection blurb cache not reliably expired when collection changes
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h2. Steps to reproduce

# Create a new collection
# Wait a few minutes
# Go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections] and make sure the collection shows up
# Edit the collection to be moderated
## Follow the “Edit” button on its blurb
## Check “This collection is moderated”
## Press “Submit”
# Immediately go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections]
# Filter the page to show only moderated collections
# Observe that the collection doesn’t show up yet
# Wait a few minutes
# Refresh the page
# Observe that the collection shows up

h2. What happens

The collection shows up, so the Elasticsearch data is updated, but the blurb still says “Unmoderated”.

h2. What should happen

Once the Elasticsearch data is updated, the blurb cache should also be refreshed so that it shows the latest information, so that the collection is “Moderated”.

h2. Development notes

This can be achieved by expiring the cache in {{self.successful_reindex(ids)}} on the Collection, since the collection blurb uses data directly from Elasticsearch.

h2. Deploy notes

Workers need to be restarted.

column1: Remove CollectionSweeper class and move callbacks to appropriate models
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
If anything vaguely related to collections changes, then the CollectionSweeper is overeager and updates caches that don’t need updating. Furthermore, we’d like to move away from sweepers generally. So let’s delete the sweeper and move its autocomplete and cache expiry callbacks into the model classes (either directly or via a concern), if they’re still needed.

Not all callbacks are still needed: For example, the collection profile does not show anything related to works, and the collection blurb pulls the works count from Elasticsearch (which uses its own collection index and collection blurb cache expiry mechanisms), so no callbacks on the work need to directly update the collection blurb. As another example, editing the collection profile currently expires the collection blurb, despite that being entirely unrelated.

Note that some lists of collection blurbs display information mostly from Elasticsearch via CollectionDecorator, while others mostly pull information directly from the database.

h2. Testing instructions

# Create a collection
# Wait a few minutes, then Browse > Collections
# Your newly created collection should show up
# Open a work that you own
# Press “Add to Collections”
# Enter part of the collection name into the “Collection name(s):” field. The collection should show up in the autocomplete
# Select the collection from the autocomplete and add the work to the collection by pressing “Add”
# Wait a few minutes, then Browse > Collections
# The collection blurb should show “Works: 1”
# Edit the collection name to be something completely different

# Press “Add to Collections”
# Enter part of the new collection name into the “Collection name(s):” field. The collection should show up in the autocomplete

column1: Drafts created in February are deleted prior to displayed date
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h2. What happens:

Drafts created in February have a displayed warning message for deletion that is set “29 days” after the draft was first created. However, the task that deletes the draft checks for drafts that are “1 month” old. In February → March, that means that drafts will be deleted one day prior to the date shown in the warning message (rather than 1-2 days after the warning, for other months).

h2. What should happen:

The draft should not be deleted until after the warning date. The rake task should use “30 days” instead of “1 month” as the time frame to delete. 

Also, the warning message on the user’s drafts page (https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/works/drafts) currently says {{Unposted drafts are only saved for a month from the day they are first created, and then deleted from the Archive.}}

This should be changed to: {{Unposted drafts are only saved for 30 days from the day they are first created, and then deleted from AO3.}}

h2. Testing:

An automated test should verify that drafts made in February are deleted at the correct time. No manual testing because we haven’t discovered time travel yet.

column1: Do not submit comments to spamchecker if they're already considered spam
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
For various reasons, we sometimes end up marking comments as spam that are already marked as spam (or are marked as deleted). While that’s not a big problem, it’s also not quite proper, so let’s change this:

The {{Comment#submit_spam}} method should be adjusted to check whether the comment is already {{approved = false}} or {{is_deleted = true}} and not submit the comment in that case. To make this work, the {{Comment#mark_as_spam!}} method has to be reordered to set the spam properties _after_ submitting the comment as spam.

(If [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5997|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5997|smart-link]  is already deployed, then {{submit_spam}} should check {{spam = true}} instead.)

h2. Testing instructions

We can’t really test this manually, but let’s at least test that we can still mark comments as spam:

# Log in
# Post a work with guest comments enabled
# Log out
# Comment on the work
# Log back in
# Navigate to the work and press the “Spam” button on the comment

The comment should be marked as spam and no longer be visible on the work.

column1: List user creations by date, not by pseud
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
When listing [all creations by a user|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/8315992136dcc81eba08755a522e4fb30d15b64c/app/controllers/admin/admin_users_controller.rb#L24] (on the creations page and the spamban confirmation page), the works and comments are grouped by pseud, which means that newer works or comments may be listed before older ones. We’d like for all works and comments on these pages to be sorted by ID/creation date instead. 

h2. Testing

# Create a pseud that alphabetizes before your username/default pseud.
# Post a work titled “Work 1 pseud A” and associate it with your new pseud. 
# Post a work titled “Work 2 default pseud” and associate it with your default pseud. 
# Post a work titled “Work 3 default pseud” and associate it with your default pseud. 
# Post a work titled “Work 4 pseud A” and associate it with your new pseud. 
# On the work you created in step 5, comment “Comment 1 on work 4, default pseud” and list it under your default pseud.

column1: Don't attach HTML of work to Abuse ticket when reporting bookmarks
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
When an abuse report is submitted for a URL containing both:

* a work ID and/or chapter ID
* a bookmark ID or page (e.g. /works/###/bookmarks/### or /works/###/bookmarks)

the HTML download of the work should not be attached to the Zoho ticket, because the reported page is solely about the bookmark(s), not the work the bookmark is on.

The HTML download of the work should still be included on work URLs such as: 
/works/###bookmark-form

h2. Development note

This should just be a matter of excluding the URL pattern in {{AbuseReport#reported_work_id}}, similar to how it’s done for comments.

column1: Spec tests create models and files that persist after they finish
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Browse > Collections > New Collection
# Fill in the required fields
# Select “Prompt Meme” from “Type of challenge, if any”
# Press “Submit”
# Fill the “Sign-up closes:” field with a date in the near future
# Select a different time zone than UTC (e.g. Alaska)
# Press “Submit”
# Wait a few minutes
# Browse > Collections, and make sure the collection shows up
# Write down how the sign-up closes date shows up for the collection you created (e.g. {{Thu 19 Mar 2026 12:00AM AKDT}})
# Hi, username! > My Preferences
# Select a different time zone than you chose for the challenge (and not UTC) (e.g. Budapest)
# Press “Update”
# Browse > Collections

h2. What happens

The sign-up closes date on the collection you created is still displayed the same as in step 10 (e.g. {{Thu 19 Mar 2026 12:00AM AKDT}}).

h2. What should happen

The sign-up closes date should be shown with the time zone you selected in your preferences (e.g. {{Thu 19 Mar 2026 12:00AM AKDT (09:00AM CET)}}).

This happens because the date is part of the collection blurb cache. To avoid the issue we can separate the cache into two parts and not cache the date in the middle between the two parts, similar to [what comments do|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3463]. This should not have an impact on how many database queries we do, because the uncached lines for the user related action buttons already query the challenge.

The second paragraph of the email says, “If you made this request, please [use this link to choose a new password|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/password/edit?reset_password_token=fakeToken] within 7 days.”

There should be separate translations for each use, e.g. {{choose_new_password_imperative: use this link to choose a new password}} and {{choose_new_password_modal: use this link to choose a new password}}. (Note: You don’t have to use those key names.)

column1: i18n SearchHelper#search_header
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
{{search_header}} currently commits a number of i18n crimes:

* pluralisation happens through {{pluralize}} doing a best guess, instead of being explicitly defined per locale or using the generic {{:many}} plural
* it blindly concatenates strings with no regards to different locales having different word orders
* it simply inserts a word into another string instead of creating separate locale key variants for separate item types

And possibly more. It would be nice to fix all of these problems all at once, and make a proper i18ned function out of {{search_header}}. This may require a rather large rewrite, possibly splitting up the method or restructuring it in other ways, whatever works best. The subscription email has some examples for how a situation with many different key variants can be properly handled for i18n, and the [general i18n standards|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Internationalization-(i18n)-Standards] may also provide some guidance.

DMCA & TIDA Policies

As the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW) is a U.S. nonprofit, we are subject to U.S. law. Content that is made available on any of our sites, including the Archive of Our Own (AO3), may therefore be subject to removal under certain conditions. In order to enact removal of content under the policies described on this page, a statutorily valid takedown notice must be submitted by an individual with the legal right to request removal of the content in question. We will not uphold removal requests from unauthorized third parties.

Table of Contents

DMCA Policy

  • My work was posted on AO3 without my permission. What can I do?
    • Filing a DMCA takedown notice
    • Requirements of a DMCA takedown notice
    • DMCA takedown process
  • I was notified that my work was removed from AO3 due to a DMCA takedown notice. What can I do?
    • Filing a DMCA counternotice
    • Requirements of a DMCA counternotice
    • DMCA counter-notification process

TIDA Policy

  • A sexually explicit photorealistic image depicting me was posted on AO3 without my consent. What can I do?
    • Filing a TIDA removal request
    • Requirements of a TIDA removal request
    • TIDA takedown process
  • I was notified that my work was removed from AO3 due to a TIDA removal request. What can I do?

Repeat Offenses

DMCA Policy

The Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) establishes the procedure the OTW will follow when users of our sites (including AO3) reproduce copyrighted material without authorization, if the infringing material is reported to us by the copyright owner or someone legally authorized to act on their behalf.

The OTW adheres to 17 U.S.C. § 512 and will respond promptly to notices of alleged copyright infringement that substantially comply with all legal requirements. However, we believe that transformative fanworks are legal, and we reserve the right to review the allegedly infringing content and independently determine whether it is infringing. If you have any questions about the OTW's DMCA Policy, please contact the Legal committee.

My work was posted on AO3 without my permission. What can I do?

If you encounter content on AO3 that you believe infringes on your copyrighted work, you have the following options:

  • Submit an Abuse report: Abuse reports are evaluated by the Policy & Abuse committee for violations of the AO3 Terms of Service, and held to a very high standard of confidentiality. When submitting an Abuse report about plagiarism or copyright infringement, you must provide a link to the violating content on AO3 and clearly identify the original source in your report description. For more information, please refer to the Terms of Service FAQ.
  • File a DMCA takedown notice: DMCA takedown notices can only be filed by the copyright owner or someone legally authorized to act on their behalf. DMCA notices must be sent to the OTW's designated agent and comply with all legal requirements. DMCA notices are not subject to confidentiality. The OTW reserves the right to make public all DMCA notices that we receive, though information may be redacted for privacy.

Please do not submit an Abuse report if you intend to file a DMCA notice. Submitting both an Abuse report and a DMCA notice about the same content may delay the processing of your request.

Filing a DMCA takedown notice

To initiate a formal DMCA takedown request, contact the OTW's designated agent using the Legal committee's contact form, via email to legal@transformativeworks.org, or by mailing a letter to:

Organization for Transformative Works
228 Park Ave S #18156
New York, NY 10003-1502
Attention: Legal

We prefer to receive DMCA requests through the contact form or by email.

Requirements of a DMCA takedown notice

The takedown notice must substantially comply with the requirements of 17 U.S.C. § 512(c)(3)(A). You are also required to consent to the jurisdiction of a United States court. The legal requirements of a valid DMCA takedown notice include:

  1. your physical or electronic signature;
  2. your contact information;
  3. identification of the copyrighted work being infringed upon (for example, a URL or publication listing);
  4. the URL(s) of the specific content on our site that you believe to be infringing;
  5. a statement that you have a good-faith belief that the use of the content is not authorized by the copyright owner(s), their agent, or the law;
    1. a statement, made under penalty of perjury, that you are authorized to act on behalf of the copyright owner; and
    2. a statement that the information you have provided is accurate.

Per 17 U.S.C. § 512(f), you may be subject to liability if you knowingly and materially misrepresent your claim that the content infringes on your copyright.

DMCA takedown process

If the OTW receives a DMCA takedown notice that fulfills all legal requirements, we will remove the content once we review the validity of the infringement claim.

When the content is removed from AO3, the information you provided in the DMCA takedown notice will be forwarded to the owner of the account responsible for posting the content. We may also send a redacted version of the DMCA takedown notice to Lumen and other third parties at our discretion.

If the account owner believes that their content does not infringe upon your copyright, they may file a DMCA counternotice disputing the takedown. The account owner can file a DMCA counternotice at any point after the content has been removed; there is no time limit.

If the OTW receives a valid DMCA counternotice, we will make reasonable efforts to notify you. You will have 10 business days to file a lawsuit to prevent the restoration of the content. If you do not notify us within 10 business days that you have filed a lawsuit, we may allow the content to be restored in accordance with 17 U.S.C. § 512(g)(2)(B)-(C).

I was notified that my work was removed from AO3 due to a DMCA takedown notice. What can I do?

Copyright infringement and plagiarism are violations of Sections II.D. and II.E. of our Terms of Service, respectively. For more information, please refer to our Terms of Service FAQ.

If the OTW receives a valid DMCA takedown notice for content you uploaded to AO3, we will remove the content and notify you by email. We may also send a redacted version of the DMCA takedown notice to Lumen and other third parties at our discretion.

If your content was removed due to a DMCA takedown notice, you cannot reupload or repost the content unless you have filed a DMCA counternotice to dispute the takedown. If you reupload or repost the content without filing a DMCA counternotice, we may suspend your account.

Filing a DMCA counternotice

If you believe that your content does not infringe on the copyright owner's work, you can file a DMCA counternotice to dispute the takedown. By filing a counternotice, you are indicating that you are willing to defend your use of the original copyrighted material in court if the party who submitted the original takedown notice chooses to pursue legal action against you.

If you are considering whether to file a DMCA counternotice, we recommend that you contact an intellectual property lawyer licensed to practice in your jurisdiction, so that you are aware of your legal rights and obligations. You can also review the Lumen DMCA Explanation and FAQ.

To initiate a formal DMCA counter-notification request, contact the OTW's designated agent using the Legal committee's contact form, via email to legal@transformativeworks.org, or by mailing a letter to:

Organization for Transformative Works
228 Park Ave S #18156
New York, NY 10003-1502
Attention: Legal

We prefer to receive DMCA requests through the contact form or by email.

You can file a DMCA counternotice at any point after your content has been removed; there is no time limit.

Requirements of a DMCA counternotice

The counternotice must substantially comply with the requirements of 17 U.S.C. § 512(g)(3). You are also required to consent to the jurisdiction of a United States court. The legal requirements of a valid DMCA counternotice include:

  1. your physical or electronic signature;
  2. your name, address, and phone number;
  3. the URL(s) of the content that was removed;
  4. a statement, made under penalty of perjury, that the content was removed due to a mistake or misidentification;
  5. a statement that you consent to the jurisdiction of a U.S. federal court in either:
    1. the district where you live, if you are in the U.S.; or
    2. the district where the OTW is located (Manhattan, New York), if you are not in the U.S.; and
  6. a statement that you will accept service of process from the party who submitted the original takedown notice.

Per 17 U.S.C. § 512(f), you may be subject to liability if you knowingly and materially misrepresent your claim that the content was removed due to a mistake or misidentification.

DMCA counter-notification process

If the OTW receives a valid DMCA counternotice, we will make reasonable efforts to notify the party who submitted the original takedown notice.

The original submitter will have 10 business days to prevent the restoration of your content by filing a lawsuit against you. If the original submitter does not file a lawsuit within 10 business days, the OTW may restore your content (or, if your content has already been deleted, allow you to reupload it) between 10 and 14 business days after we receive the counternotice. We may also send a redacted version of the DMCA counternotice to Lumen and other third parties at our discretion.

TIDA Policy

The "Tools to Address Known Exploitation by Immobilizing Technological Deepfakes on Websites and Networks Act" (Take It Down Act, or TIDA) establishes the procedure the OTW will follow when users of our sites (including AO3) embed or link to nonconsensual, sexually explicit photorealistic images of an identifiable individual, if the images are reported to us by the depicted individual or by someone legally authorized to act on their behalf.

A sexually explicit photorealistic image depicting me was posted on AO3 without my consent. What can I do?

If you encounter a sexually explicit or suggestive photograph, video, photorealistic computer-generated image (including "deepfakes" and "AI" images), or other photorealistic image on AO3 that could potentially be mistaken for an actual photograph or video of you in a sexually explicit context, you have the following options:

  • File a TIDA removal request with the OTW: TIDA removal requests can only be filed by the individual depicted in the image or by someone legally authorized to act on their behalf. TIDA removal requests must be sent to the OTW's designated agent and comply with all legal requirements.
  • File a TIDA removal request with the image host: Because images embedded in works are not hosted on AO3, filing a TIDA removal request with the OTW will not remove the image itself from the internet. You may therefore wish to contact the image host directly and file your removal request with them. If the hosting service removes the image, the image will no longer appear on any site, including AO3.
Filing a TIDA removal request

A TIDA removal request can be filed for photographs, videos, or other images (including "deepfakes" and "AI" images) that are sexually explicit or suggestive, "indistinguishable from an authentic visual depiction", and published without the consent of the person depicted in the image. To initiate a TIDA removal request, the depicted person or their legal representative must contact the OTW's designated agent using the Legal committee's contact form or via email to legal@transformativeworks.org. Submitters should be prepared to present proof that they are the depicted person or their legal representative. We will not process third-party complaints.

Requirements of a TIDA removal request

A valid TIDA removal request must include:

  1. a physical or electronic signature of the identifiable individual (or an authorized person acting on their behalf);
  2. contact information for the identifiable individual (or an authorized person acting on their behalf);
  3. the URL(s) on our site where the image(s) can be found;
  4. a statement, made by the identifiable individual (or an authorized person acting on their behalf), that they are requesting to remove the image(s) because:
    1. the image(s) in question are photorealistic, sexually explicit, and identifiably depict the named individual; and
    2. they have a good-faith belief that the image(s) were published without the consent of the identifiable individual.
TIDA takedown process

If the OTW receives a TIDA removal request that fulfills all legal requirements, we will remove the content once we review the validity of the claim.

When the content is removed from AO3, we will make reasonable efforts to notify the owner of the account responsible for posting the content.

If the account owner believes that their content does not violate the Take It Down Act, they may appeal by responding to the removal notice and explaining which elements do not apply. Appeals will be resolved at the sole discretion of the OTW.

I was notified that my work contained images that were subject to removal under the Take It Down Act. What can I do?

If the OTW receives a valid TIDA removal request for images featured in content you posted on AO3, we will remove the content and make reasonable efforts to notify you by email.

If your content was removed due to a TIDA takedown notice, you have the following options:

  • Remove the images from your work: Because the Take It Down Act only applies to images, you can remove the linked or embedded images that were the subject of the TIDA removal request. As long as your work does not otherwise violate the Terms of Service, we may restore your content (or, if your content has already been deleted, allow you to reupload it).
  • Submit an appeal: If you believe the TIDA takedown notice was invalid, you can appeal the removal of the images by replying to the notification email. You will need to explain which elements of the original TIDA removal request do not apply to your situation. Appeals will be resolved at the sole discretion of the OTW.

If you reupload or repost the content without removing the linked or embedded images, or without your appeal being granted, we may suspend your account.

Repeat Offenses

As required by 17 U.S.C. § 512(i)(1)(A), we may suspend users who repeatedly violate others' copyright. We may also suspend users who repeatedly post images in violation of the Take It Down Act. The OTW has the discretion to decide what qualifies as a repeated offense.

When an admin setting up two-step verification for their account, we want there to be a button next to the setup code (underneath the QR code) that copies it to the clipboard. # Log in as an admin (any role will work).
## If you are already logged in, click the “Hi, admin-name” button in the top right of the page.
# If have two-step verification enabled, disable it.
# Click the {{Set up two-step verification with an authenticator app}} link.
## Enter your password to continue.
## You should see a button next to the setup code that says {{Copy}}. Click it.
## The text on the button should change to {{Copied!}}
## Open your preferred text editor and paste from the clipboard (ctrl+v or command+v).
## The setup code (the long string of characters under the QR code) from the page should be pasted into the editor.

# Disable two-step verification and JavaScript.
# Repeat steps 3 and 3a.
## You should not see a button that says {{Copy}}.

When a work is unrevealed, the work blurb and the header module inside the blurb have the {{mystery}} class. 

There is currently no corresponding class for works that are anonymous, so we’d like to add an  {{anonymous}} class in the same places. 

We can also add it to series blurbs and the header module inside the series blurb for consistency.

h1. Testing

h2. Setup

# Log in
# Update your preferences to allow gifts
## Hi, username! > My Preferences
## Check “Allow anyone to gift me works.”
## Press “Update”
# Create an anonymous collection

## Check “This collection is anonymous”
## Press “Submit”
# Post a work in a series to the anonymous collection

## Fill in required information

## Check “This work is part of a series”

## Press “Post”

## Press “Create”
# Bookmark the series
## Follow the link to the series from the work blurb
## Press the “Bookmark” button
## Press “Create”
# Create a skin to highlight anonymous things
## Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins > New Site Skin
## Fill in required information
## For the CSS, add an obvious border to anything with the {{anonymous}} class, like {{.anonymous { border: 2px dashed DarkOrchid !important; }}}. 
## Press “Submit”
## Press “Use”

Leave the pages from Steps 1-5 open; you’ll need them in Step 6.

# The work blurb should have the anonymous class on the blurb and the header module inside the blurb, meaning you’ll see an outer and inner border. You can check the work blurb on your Works in Collections page: {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/works/collected}}

You can check these blurbs on your bookmarks page: {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/bookmarks}}
